# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/^1/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`by hand, and switching from handwritten impls to thiserror or vice versa is not a breaking change.
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display`impl is generated for your error if you provide`#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {})", i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From`impl is generated for each variant that contains a`#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()`method is implemented to return whichever field has a`#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()`method is implemented to provide whichever field has a type named`Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace`. Using`Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()`method is forwarded to the source’s`provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and Display methods straight through to an underlying error without adding an additional message. This would be appropriate for enums that need an “anything else” variant.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

# xpile_contracts - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-contracts/^0.1.12/

## Expand description

xpile contracts — provable-contracts integration.

xpile delegates its entire contract framework to
[ provable-contracts](https://github.com/paiml/aprender/tree/main/crates/aprender-contracts)
(the

`aprender-contracts` crate, library name `provable_contracts`).
See `docs/specifications/xpile-contract-driven-design-v1.md` for the
design rationale.This crate re-exports the upstream framework and adds xpile-specific
helpers — primarily the `XpileContractLayer` enum that tags each
contract by taxonomy layer (language semantics / translation /
architectural / hybrid pipeline).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [audit](https://docs.rs/audit/index.html)
- Audit trail generator — traceability chain.
- [binding](https://docs.rs/binding/index.html)
- Binding registry — maps contract equations to implementations.
- [book_](https://docs.rs/book_gen/index.html)- gen
- mdBook page generation for contracts.
- [coverage](https://docs.rs/coverage/index.html)
- Cross-contract obligation coverage report.
- [diff](https://docs.rs/diff/index.html)
- Contract diff — detect drift between contract versions.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [generate](https://docs.rs/generate/index.html)
- End-to-end codegen — generates all artifacts to disk.
- [graph](https://docs.rs/graph/index.html)
- Contract dependency graph — composition via `depends_on`.
- [infer](https://docs.rs/infer/index.html)
- Contract inference engine.
- [kani_](https://docs.rs/kani_gen/index.html)- gen
- Kani harness generator — Phase 6 of the pipeline.
- [latex](https://docs.rs/latex/index.html)
- LaTeX conversion utilities for contract math notation.
- [lean_](https://docs.rs/lean_gen/index.html)- gen
- Lean 4 code generator — Phase 7 of the pipeline.
- [lint](https://docs.rs/lint/index.html)
- Contract quality gate: validate + audit + score in one pass.
- [probar_](https://docs.rs/probar_gen/index.html)- gen
- Probar property-test generator — Phase 5 of the pipeline.
- [query](https://docs.rs/query/index.html)
- Contract query engine with BM25 semantic search.
- [readme_](https://docs.rs/readme_gen/index.html)- gen
- Deterministic README.md and CI workflow generation for consumer projects.
- [scaffold](https://docs.rs/scaffold/index.html)
- Scaffold generator — Phase 3 of the pipeline.
- [schema](https://docs.rs/schema/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

parsed contract carries equations, proof obligations, falsification

# xpile_contract_frontend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-contract-frontend/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_contract_frontend/

## Expand description

ContractFrontend trait — proof-lane parsing abstraction.

Parses notation (LaTeX math + theorem environments, Lean 4 theorem
text, mdBook with embedded math) into contract equation YAML.
Sibling of [`xpile_frontend::Frontend`]; the proof lane is disjoint
from the code lane and does NOT produce meta-HIR.

Architectural invariants codified in
`contracts/xpile-contract-frontend-trait-v1.yaml`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Equation](https://docs.rs/struct.Equation.html)
- A single equation parsed from notation, in canonical YAML form.
- [Equations](https://docs.rs/struct.EquationsBlock.html)- Block
- Result of parsing a notation source into the proof-lane contract
substrate. `equations_only`invariant: NO meta-HIR is produced or mutated by ContractFrontend implementations.
- [Proof](https://docs.rs/struct.ProofObligation.html)- Obligation
- A single proof obligation parsed from a theorem-class environment.

# xpile_meta_hir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/^0.1.12/

## Expand description

Canonical meta-HIR.

Every frontend in xpile lowers its language-specific AST to this
shared, intentionally minimal IR. The federated approach (see
`docs/specifications/xpile-architecture-v1.md`) means we start
lossy and grow as hybrid-transpile cases demand.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html)
- [FfiBoundary](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiBoundary.html)
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html)
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.Module.html)
- [Param](https://docs.rs/struct.Param.html)
- [SortKey](https://docs.rs/struct.SortKey.html)
- PMAT-502z (Tranche 2): a `sorted(xs, key=lambda p: e)`sort key — the lambda’s single parameter name plus its (already-lowered) body. The body is lowered with`param`left unbound (an`Ident`), so it works for bodies that don’t need the param’s precise static type (arithmetic,`len(p)`, most builtins); the backend emits`let <param> = __k.clone();`to bind it by value at runtime. Str-method keys (`p.upper()`) are deferred.
- [TryHandler](https://docs.rs/struct.TryHandler.html)
- PMAT-1059: one `except`clause of a multi-handler statement-form`Stmt::TryCatch``as <name>`message binding, and handler statement block.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [BinOp](https://docs.rs/enum.BinOp.html)
- [Dict](https://docs.rs/enum.DictViewKind.html)- View - Kind
- PMAT-502v (Tranche 2): dict view methods carried by `Expr::DictView`
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)
- [FloatOp](https://docs.rs/enum.FloatOp.html)
- PMAT-477 (R8): float arithmetic operators. Carried by
`Expr::FloatBinOp``Add`/`Sub`/`Mul`/`Div`emit plain infix (`f64`saturates, no`checked_*`);`Div`is IEEE-754 true division. PMAT-502br:`FloorDiv`/`Mod`emit Python-correct*floor*semantics (`(a / b).floor()`and`a - b * (a / b).floor()`), which differ from Rust’s truncating`/`int-div and sign-of-dividend`%`— so they are NOT plain infix.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/enum.Item.html)
- [List](https://docs.rs/enum.ListMutateOp.html)- Mutate - Op
- PMAT-502ap (Tranche 2): no-argument in-place list mutators carried by
`Stmt::ListMutate``Vec`method; all return`None`in Python (so they only appear as expression statements).
- [List](https://docs.rs/enum.ListQueryOp.html)- Query - Op
- PMAT-502u (Tranche 2): list query methods carried by `Expr::ListQuery``Int`;`Index`panics on a missing element (Python`ValueError`).
- [Loop](https://docs.rs/enum.LoopKind.html)- Kind
- POSIX shell loop dialects. PMAT-048 / XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001
Layer B. Each variant carries the loop’s control predicate /
item list; the body lives in `Stmt::ShellLoop::body`.
- [NumBuiltin](https://docs.rs/enum.NumBuiltinOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-498 (Tranche 2): scalar numeric builtins carried by
`Expr::NumBuiltin``Abs`takes 1 arg;`Min`/`Max`are variadic (`>= 2`args, PMAT-502cz) and chain`.min`/`.max`over the tail.
- [Pair](https://docs.rs/enum.PairIterKind.html)- Iter - Kind
- PMAT-495 (sprint): the iterator adapter for a `Stmt::ForEachPair`
- [Quoting](https://docs.rs/enum.QuotingStrategy.html)- Strategy
- Per-arg shell quoting choice. Carried by `Expr::QuotedString`so the bashrs-backend renders each arg in the strategy the source indicated. v0.1.0’s bashrs-frontend doesn’t have a real quoting-aware parser yet — it produces`Expr::LitStr`for every arg, and`QuotingStrategy::None`is implicit there. The full strategy set is wired so the v0.2.0 source fold’s real bashrs parser can plug in without IR churn.
- [Radix](https://docs.rs/enum.Radix.html)
- PMAT-502cv: the radix for `hex`/`oct`/`bin`(`Expr::IntRadixStr`).
- [SetOp](https://docs.rs/enum.SetOp.html)
- PMAT-502g (Tranche 2): set-algebra operators carried by `Expr::SetOp``HashSet`method that returns an iterator of borrows, materialized via`.cloned().collect()`into a new owned`HashSet`.
- [SetPred](https://docs.rs/enum.SetPredOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-502ep (Tranche 2): set predicates carried by `Expr::SetPred``bool`. Each maps to a`HashSet`query method; the proper variants additionally require the sets to differ.
- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.SourceLang.html)- Lang
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)
- [StrMethod](https://docs.rs/enum.StrMethodOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-492 (sprint): no-argument Python string transform methods,
carried by `Expr::StrMethod`
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.Type.html)
- MVP type lattice. Will grow as frontends demand it. Keep semantically
minimal; map source-language type idiosyncrasies (Python int bigint
promotion, C signed/unsigned, etc.) at the frontend boundary.
PMAT-455 — `Type`is no longer`Copy`because`Type::List(Box<Type>)`is heap-allocated. Callers that previously relied on`*ty`to dereference / copy now use`.clone()`(cheap — most Type values are leaf variants or 1-deep boxes).
- [UnOp](https://docs.rs/enum.UnOp.html)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [collect_](https://docs.rs/fn.collect_block_idents.html)- block_ - idents
- PMAT-736 (HUNT-V11 V11-6): collect every identifier-position name reachable
from `block`into`acc`— both value references (`Expr::Ident`, a`Call`callee) and receiver names (`xs.append(...)`’s`xs`,`d[k] = v`’s`d`, …), plus binding names (a`let`, a loop var). It is the read-only mirror of the`escape_*`walker above: every`escape_name(x)`there becomes`acc.insert(x)`here, so the two stay structurally identical (both are compiler-checked exhaustive over`Stmt`/`Expr`). Used by the frontend’s nested-function lowering to decide whether a nested`def`is self-recursive and whether it captures an enclosing local — over-collection (a binding name, a lambda param) is harmless there, since the caller only intersects the result with the enclosing scope.
- [escape_](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_rust_reserved_idents.html)- rust_ - reserved_ - idents
- PMAT-573: rewrite every identifier in `module`that collides with a Rust keyword to its raw form`r#kw`, so Python locals/params/functions named`type`/`match`/`loop`/… emit valid Rust (and Ruchy). The Rust-family backends call this on a*cloned*module before emission. Struct/enum type names, struct field names, and method names are left unescaped (a keyword-named class/field/method is a separate, rarer fidelity gap).
- [retype_](https://docs.rs/fn.retype_ffi_float_call_sites.html)- ffi_ - float_ - call_ - sites
- Re-type the call sites of `float_ffi`FFI symbols in`module`to F64 so the float-repr path (print`.0`,`let: f64`, float return) is selected. See the PMAT-931 block above. No-op when`float_ffi`is empty.

[107](https://docs.rs#107)/// PMAT-901: the `build.rs` emitted into a hybrid workspace. std-only: it
[108](https://docs.rs#108)/// `cc`-compiles every `csrc/*.c` to an object and links it directly into the
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// binary via `cargo:rustc-link-arg`, so the emitted `extern "C"` shims resolve
[110](https://docs.rs#110)/// against the real C symbols at link time (objects passed directly are fully
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// included — no archive/`ar` needed).
[112](https://docs.rs#112)const HYBRID_BUILD_RS: &str = r#"// Generated by xpile hybrid (Phase 5a) — do not edit.
[113](https://docs.rs#113)fn main() {
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    let out_dir = std::env::var("OUT_DIR").expect("OUT_DIR");
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    let manifest = std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR");
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    let csrc = std::path::Path::new(&manifest).join("csrc");
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&csrc) {
[118](https://docs.rs#118)        Ok(e) => e,
[119](https://docs.rs#119)        Err(_) => return,
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    };
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    for entry in entries.flatten() {
[122](https://docs.rs#122)        let path = entry.path();
[123](https://docs.rs#123)        if path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) != Some("c") {
[124](https://docs.rs#124)            continue;
[125](https://docs.rs#125)        }
[126](https://docs.rs#126)        let stem = path.file_stem().unwrap().to_string_lossy().to_string();
[127](https://docs.rs#127)        let obj = format!("{out_dir}/{stem}.o");
[128](https://docs.rs#128)        let status = std::process::Command::new("cc")
[129](https://docs.rs#129)            .arg("-c")
[130](https://docs.rs#130)            .arg(&path)
[131](https://docs.rs#131)            .arg("-o")
[132](https://docs.rs#132)            .arg(&obj)
[133](https://docs.rs#133)            .status()
[134](https://docs.rs#134)            .expect("spawn cc");
[135](https://docs.rs#135)        assert!(status.success(), "cc failed on {}", path.display());
[136](https://docs.rs#136)        println!("cargo:rustc-link-arg={obj}");
[137](https://docs.rs#137)        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", path.display());
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    }

[142](https://docs.rs#142)/// Deterministic, dependency-free shim id (FNV-1a hex over the boundary's
[143](https://docs.rs#143)/// identifying fields). Stable across runs so a manifest entry — and the shim it
[144](https://docs.rs#144)/// names — is reproducible. (The spec's sha256 is a later hardening; FNV-1a is
[145](https://docs.rs#145)/// sufficient for in-session uniqueness and is std-only.)
[146](https://docs.rs#146)/// PMAT-895 (Sprint-2 Tier 2): the externally-callable name a module item
[147](https://docs.rs#147)/// exports — what an incoming FFI boundary's `symbol` must match. A callable FFI
[148](https://docs.rs#148)/// symbol is a function; a module-level constant is also addressable. Structs/
[149](https://docs.rs#149)/// enums are types, not call targets, so they don't export an FFI symbol.
[150](https://docs.rs#150)fn item_exported_name(item: &Item) -> Option<&str> {
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    match item {
[152](https://docs.rs#152)        Item::Function(f) => Some(&f.name),
[153](https://docs.rs#153)        Item::Const { name, .. } => Some(name),
[154](https://docs.rs#154)        _ => None,
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    }
[156](https://docs.rs#156)}
[157](https://docs.rs#157)
[158](https://docs.rs#158)/// PMAT-932: does `module` export `symbol` as an FFI-callable target?
[159](https://docs.rs#159)///
[160](https://docs.rs#160)/// For a code module (C/Python/C++/Ruchy/Rust) the callable surface is its
[161](https://docs.rs#161)/// exported items — a function or addressable const named `symbol`. A **Shell**
[162](https://docs.rs#162)/// module is different: a shell script is invoked *as a subprocess by its program
[163](https://docs.rs#163)/// name*, which `bashrs-frontend` records as the `Module::name` (the file stem),
[164](https://docs.rs#164)/// not as a meta-HIR `Item` (its only synthetic item is the structural `main`
[165](https://docs.rs#165)/// placeholder). The thing the Python side actually calls — and the thing
[166](https://docs.rs#166)/// [`emit_shell_shim`] spawns via `Command::new(symbol)` — is that program name.
[167](https://docs.rs#167)/// So a Shell module "exports" the symbol equal to its module name. This is what
[168](https://docs.rs#168)/// makes the Python→Shell boundary resolvable end-to-end (the `emit_shell_shim`
[169](https://docs.rs#169)/// arm had no producer before this — `C-FFI-SHELL-SUBPROCESS`).
[170](https://docs.rs#170)fn module_exports_symbol(m: &Module, symbol: &str) -> bool {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    match m.source_lang {
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        // Shell tools are addressed by their program (script) name.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        SourceLang::Shell => m.name == symbol,
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        // Everything else exposes named items (functions / addressable consts).
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        _ => m
[176](https://docs.rs#176)            .items
[177](https://docs.rs#177)            .iter()
[178](https://docs.rs#178)            .any(|it| item_exported_name(it) == Some(symbol)),
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    }
[180](https://docs.rs#180)}
[181](https://docs.rs#181)
[182](https://docs.rs#182)fn shim_id(b: &FfiBoundary) -> String {
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    let key = format!(
[184](https://docs.rs#184)        "{:?}->{:?}:{}:{}",
[185](https://docs.rs#185)        b.from_lang, b.to_lang, b.symbol, b.signature
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    );
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    for byte in key.as_bytes() {
[189](https://docs.rs#189)        h ^= *byte as u64;
[190](https://docs.rs#190)        h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    }
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    format!("shim_{h:016x}")
[193](https://docs.rs#193)}
[194](https://docs.rs#194)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)impl FfiManifest {
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[197](https://docs.rs#197)        Self::default()
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    }
[199](https://docs.rs#199)
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    pub fn register(&mut self, entry: FfiEntry) {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)        self.entries.push(entry);
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    }
[203](https://docs.rs#203)
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// Phase 2 of the hybrid transpile flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// reconcile every cross-language FFI boundary across the dispatched modules
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    /// into a single manifest, or fail listing the unresolved boundaries.
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    ///
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    /// A boundary `{from_lang, to_lang, symbol, signature}` is a call that
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// crosses from `from_lang` into `to_lang`. It RESOLVES when a sibling module
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// of `to_lang` is present in the dispatched set (the target language was
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// actually transpiled). Each resolved boundary becomes an [`FfiEntry`] with a
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    /// deterministic `shim_id`; any boundary whose target language is absent fails
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// reconciliation (the `manifest_completeness` invariant of
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    /// `C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT`). Same-language boundaries (`from == to`) are no-ops.
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    ///
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    /// PMAT-895: resolution is SYMBOL-LEVEL — a boundary resolves only when a
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    /// module of `to_lang` actually DEFINES an item (function/const) named
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    /// `symbol`. A target-language module that is present but does NOT export the
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    /// symbol still fails reconciliation (the `manifest_completeness` invariant is
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// about the symbol crossing the line, not just the language being present).
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    pub fn reconcile(modules: &[Module]) -> Result<FfiManifest, FfiReconcileError> {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)        let mut manifest = FfiManifest::new();
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        let mut unresolved = Vec::new();
[224](https://docs.rs#224)        for module in modules {
[225](https://docs.rs#225)            for b in &module.ffi_boundaries {
[226](https://docs.rs#226)                if b.from_lang == b.to_lang {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)                    continue; // not a cross-language boundary
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                }
[229](https://docs.rs#229)                let lang_present = modules.iter().any(|m| m.source_lang == b.to_lang);
[230](https://docs.rs#230)                let symbol_defined = modules.iter().any(|m| {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)                    m.source_lang == b.to_lang && module_exports_symbol(m, b.symbol.as_str())
[232](https://docs.rs#232)                });
[233](https://docs.rs#233)                if symbol_defined {
[234](https://docs.rs#234)                    manifest.register(FfiEntry {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)                        symbol: b.symbol.clone(),
[236](https://docs.rs#236)                        from_lang: b.from_lang,
[237](https://docs.rs#237)                        to_lang: b.to_lang,
[238](https://docs.rs#238)                        source_signature: b.signature.clone(),
[239](https://docs.rs#239)                        // First-cut shim signature: the real C/PyObject → Rust
[240](https://docs.rs#240)                        // lowering is a later increment; record a stable placeholder
[241](https://docs.rs#241)                        // that names the symbol so downstream emission can key on it.
[242](https://docs.rs#242)                        rust_shim_signature: format!("fn {}(/* {} */)", b.symbol, b.signature),
[243](https://docs.rs#243)                        shim_id: shim_id(b),
[244](https://docs.rs#244)                    });
[245](https://docs.rs#245)                } else {
[246](https://docs.rs#246)                    // Distinguish "no target-language module at all" from "module
[247](https://docs.rs#247)                    // present but symbol not exported" — both block the hybrid
[248](https://docs.rs#248)                    // build, but the diagnostic should point at the right fix.
[249](https://docs.rs#249)                    let reason = if lang_present {
[250](https://docs.rs#250)                        format!("no {:?} module defines `{}`", b.to_lang, b.symbol)
[251](https://docs.rs#251)                    } else {
[252](https://docs.rs#252)                        format!("no {:?} module in the dispatched set", b.to_lang)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)                    };
[254](https://docs.rs#254)                    unresolved.push(format!(
[255](https://docs.rs#255)                        "{:?}->{:?} `{}` ({}): {}",
[256](https://docs.rs#256)                        b.from_lang, b.to_lang, b.symbol, b.signature, reason
[257](https://docs.rs#257)                    ));
[258](https://docs.rs#258)                }
[259](https://docs.rs#259)            }
[260](https://docs.rs#260)        }
[261](https://docs.rs#261)        if unresolved.is_empty() {
[262](https://docs.rs#262)            Ok(manifest)
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        } else {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)            Err(FfiReconcileError { unresolved })
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        }
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    }
[267](https://docs.rs#267)
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// PMAT-899 — Phase 4 of the hybrid flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// emit a self-contained Rust FFI shim file for every reconciled
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// cross-language boundary, dispatched per target paradigm. `modules` is the
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    /// same set passed to [`reconcile`](Self::reconcile) — it is the ONLY source
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// of real param/return types (an [`FfiEntry`] carries placeholder
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    /// signatures).
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    ///
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// Per-paradigm strategy (see [`shim_part_for`]):
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    ///   - **C** → a real `extern "C"` foreign declaration + a safe `*_shim`
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    ///     wrapper confining `unsafe`, citing `C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT`.
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    ///   - **Shell** → a real `std::process::Command`-based wrapper (shell speaks
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    ///     argv + exit codes — no C ABI, no `unsafe`), citing
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    ///     `C-FFI-SHELL-SUBPROCESS`.
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    ///   - **Ruchy / Rust** → a real same-crate direct-call forwarder (both lower
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    ///     to native Rust in the same crate — a plain in-crate call, no `unsafe`,
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    ///     no `extern`).
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    ///   - **Python** → a real pyo3 CPython-embedding shim (PMAT-926): under the
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    ///     GIL it imports the defining module and calls the function, marshalling
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    ///     scalar args/return through pyo3 (`i64`/`f64`/`bool`/`String`).
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    ///   - **Cpp** → a real pybind11 C++ shim (PMAT-927): the C++ symbol is
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    ///     name-mangled, so this calls the pybind11-registered binding by its
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    ///     Python-visible name through the embedded interpreter (the same path
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    ///     Python uses), refusing rather than guessing a mangled `extern "C"`.
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    ///     Six of seven arms are now real (C, Shell, Ruchy, Rust, Python, Cpp).
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    ///   - **Cuda / Lean** → a specific, mechanism-named [`FfiEmitError`]
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    ///     (cuda_kernel / proof-lane) so the remaining gaps stay actionable,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    ///     never silently dropped or mis-emitted.
[295](https://docs.rs#295)    ///
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    /// All-or-nothing (mirrors `reconcile`'s `manifest_completeness`): if ANY
[297](https://docs.rs#297)    /// boundary cannot be shimmed, nothing is emitted and the gaps are returned —
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    /// a half-shimmed hybrid build is not a build.
[299](https://docs.rs#299)    ///
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    /// Compile-checkable WITHOUT the foreign object: a C extern symbol stays
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    /// unresolved at lib-build time and a shell shim needs no symbol at all, so
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    /// type/arity/ABI are validated by `rustc --crate-type lib` alone (linking is
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    /// only needed to *run*).
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    pub fn emit_rust_shims(&self, modules: &[Module]) -> Result<String, FfiEmitError> {
[305](https://docs.rs#305)        let mut unsupported = Vec::new();
[306](https://docs.rs#306)        let mut extern_lines = Vec::new();
[307](https://docs.rs#307)        let mut wrappers = Vec::new();
[308](https://docs.rs#308)        let mut contracts: Vec<&'static str> = Vec::new();
[309](https://docs.rs#309)
[310](https://docs.rs#310)        for entry in &self.entries {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)            match shim_part_for(entry, modules) {
[312](https://docs.rs#312)                Ok(part) => {
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                    extern_lines.extend(part.extern_decl);
[314](https://docs.rs#314)                    wrappers.push(part.wrapper);
[315](https://docs.rs#315)                    if let Some(c) = part.contract {
[316](https://docs.rs#316)                        if !contracts.contains(&c) {
[317](https://docs.rs#317)                            contracts.push(c);
[318](https://docs.rs#318)                        }
[319](https://docs.rs#319)                    }
[320](https://docs.rs#320)                }
[321](https://docs.rs#321)                Err(reasons) => unsupported.extend(reasons),
[322](https://docs.rs#322)            }
[323](https://docs.rs#323)        }
[324](https://docs.rs#324)
[325](https://docs.rs#325)        if !unsupported.is_empty() {
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            return Err(FfiEmitError { unsupported });
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        let mut out = String::new();
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        out.push_str("// Generated by xpile hybrid (Phase 4) — do not edit.\n");
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        out.push_str("// FFI shims recovered from the reconciled manifest.\n");
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        for c in &contracts {
[333](https://docs.rs#333)            out.push_str(&format!("// xpile-contract: {c}\n"));
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        }
[335](https://docs.rs#335)        if !extern_lines.is_empty() {
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            out.push_str("// ABI note: C `int` lowers to meta-HIR Type::I64 -> c_int (32-bit),\n");
[337](https://docs.rs#337)            out.push_str("//   while `long`/`int64_t` lower to the distinct Type::CLong width\n");
[338](https://docs.rs#338)            out.push_str(
[339](https://docs.rs#339)                "//   -> c_longlong (64-bit), not narrowed to c_int (PMAT-909), and `double`\n",
[340](https://docs.rs#340)            );
[341](https://docs.rs#341)            out.push_str(
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                "//   -> Type::F64 -> c_double (64-bit, PMAT-910), and `float` -> the distinct\n",
[343](https://docs.rs#343)            );
[344](https://docs.rs#344)            out.push_str(
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                "//   Type::F32 -> c_float (32-bit, PMAT-911), not widened through c_double,\n",
[346](https://docs.rs#346)            );
[347](https://docs.rs#347)            out.push_str(
[348](https://docs.rs#348)                "//   and `unsigned`/`uint32_t` -> the distinct Type::CUInt -> c_uint (32-bit\n",
[349](https://docs.rs#349)            );
[350](https://docs.rs#350)            out.push_str("//   UNSIGNED, PMAT-918), not the signed c_int,\n");
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            out.push_str(
[352](https://docs.rs#352)                "//   and `unsigned long`/`uint64_t` -> the distinct Type::CULong -> c_ulonglong\n",
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            );
[354](https://docs.rs#354)            out.push_str(
[355](https://docs.rs#355)                "//   (64-bit UNSIGNED, PMAT-921), neither the 32-bit c_uint nor the signed c_longlong,\n",
[356](https://docs.rs#356)            );
[357](https://docs.rs#357)            out.push_str(
[358](https://docs.rs#358)                "//   and a C pointer `T*` -> the distinct Type::Ptr -> a raw `*mut`/`*const <pointee>`\n",
[359](https://docs.rs#359)            );
[360](https://docs.rs#360)            out.push_str(
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                "//   (PMAT-924, the first address-carrying ABI token; `char*` -> `*mut c_char`),\n",
[362](https://docs.rs#362)            );
[363](https://docs.rs#363)            out.push_str(
[364](https://docs.rs#364)                "//   the pointee restricted to an ABI-mappable scalar (pointer-to-pointer/container\n",
[365](https://docs.rs#365)            );
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            out.push_str(
[367](https://docs.rs#367)                "//   /struct refused), and a C string `char*` MARSHALLED to/from a Rust `&str`/`String`\n",
[368](https://docs.rs#368)            );
[369](https://docs.rs#369)            out.push_str(
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                "//   via a CString/CStr round-trip (PMAT-925, the last decy ABI ceiling — the safe\n",
[371](https://docs.rs#371)            );
[372](https://docs.rs#372)            out.push_str("//   wrapper never exposes a raw `*mut c_char`).\n");
[373](https://docs.rs#373)        }
[374](https://docs.rs#374)        out.push_str("#![allow(dead_code)]\n");
[375](https://docs.rs#375)        if !extern_lines.is_empty() {
[376](https://docs.rs#376)            // `unsafe extern "C"` (not bare `extern "C"`): a bare extern block is
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            // a hard error under Rust edition 2024 (`extern blocks must be
[378](https://docs.rs#378)            // unsafe`), and `cargo new` has defaulted to edition 2024 since Rust
[379](https://docs.rs#379)            // 1.85. `unsafe extern` compiles cleanly under 2021 AND 2024, so the
[380](https://docs.rs#380)            // emitted file stays valid in whatever crate the user drops it into.
[381](https://docs.rs#381)            out.push_str("\nunsafe extern \"C\" {\n");
[382](https://docs.rs#382)            out.push_str(&extern_lines.join("\n"));
[383](https://docs.rs#383)            out.push('\n');
[384](https://docs.rs#384)            out.push_str("}\n");
[385](https://docs.rs#385)        }
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        for w in &wrappers {
[387](https://docs.rs#387)            out.push('\n');
[388](https://docs.rs#388)            out.push_str(w);
[389](https://docs.rs#389)        }
[390](https://docs.rs#390)        Ok(out)
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    /// PMAT-901 — Phase 5a of the hybrid flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    /// emit a self-contained, BUILDABLE Cargo workspace for the hybrid module.
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    /// Files: `Cargo.toml` (a bin crate); `build.rs` ([`HYBRID_BUILD_RS`] —
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    /// cc-compiles every `csrc/*.c` and links it); `csrc/<name>.c` (each C source
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    /// verbatim, from `c_sources`); `src/ffi_shims.rs` (the reconciled shims from
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// [`emit_rust_shims`](Self::emit_rust_shims)); and `src/main.rs` (`rust_src`,
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// the caller's lowering of the non-C modules, plus `mod ffi_shims;`).
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    ///
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// `cargo build` on the result compiles the Rust side AND cc-compiles + links
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    /// the C side through the emitted `extern "C"` shim — the first *executing*
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    /// hybrid artifact (Phase 5a). `rust_src` is supplied by the caller (the rust
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// backend's lowering of the entry module) so this crate stays codegen-free.
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    /// All-or-nothing: an unshimmable boundary fails via [`FfiEmitError`] before
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// anything is written past the shim step.
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    pub fn emit_hybrid_workspace(
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        &self,
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        modules: &[Module],
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        c_sources: &[(String, String)],
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        rust_src: &str,
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        out_dir: &Path,
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    ) -> Result<(), WorkspaceEmitError> {
[414](https://docs.rs#414)        // Fail loud on an unshimmable boundary BEFORE touching the filesystem.
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        let shims = self.emit_rust_shims(modules)?;
[416](https://docs.rs#416)
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        std::fs::create_dir_all(out_dir.join("src"))?;
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        std::fs::create_dir_all(out_dir.join("csrc"))?;
[419](https://docs.rs#419)        std::fs::write(
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            out_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
[421](https://docs.rs#421)            "[package]\nname = \"xpile-hybrid-artifact\"\nversion = \"0.0.0\"\nedition = \"2021\"\n\n[dependencies]\n",
[422](https://docs.rs#422)        )?;
[423](https://docs.rs#423)        std::fs::write(out_dir.join("build.rs"), HYBRID_BUILD_RS)?;
[424](https://docs.rs#424)        for (name, content) in c_sources {
[425](https://docs.rs#425)            std::fs::write(out_dir.join("csrc").join(name), content)?;
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        }
[427](https://docs.rs#427)        std::fs::write(out_dir.join("src").join("ffi_shims.rs"), &shims)?;
[428](https://docs.rs#428)        // PMAT-902: bridge the lowered call names to the emitted shims. The Python
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        // frontend lowers a boundary call `square_sum(7)` to a plain `square_sum(7)`,
[430](https://docs.rs#430)        // but the safe wrapper is `ffi_shims::square_sum_shim`. A per-boundary
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        // `use ffi_shims::<sym>_shim as <sym>;` makes the lowered call resolve to
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        // the shim, so an `app.py` `main()` that actually invokes the C side links
[433](https://docs.rs#433)        // and runs (the executing north-star artifact). `allow(unused_imports)`
[434](https://docs.rs#434)        // keeps a `pass`-bodied `main()` (no boundary call) warning-free.
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        let mut aliases = String::new();
[436](https://docs.rs#436)        for e in &self.entries {
[437](https://docs.rs#437)            aliases.push_str(&format!(
[438](https://docs.rs#438)                "#[allow(unused_imports)]\nuse ffi_shims::{0}_shim as {0};\n",
[439](https://docs.rs#439)                e.symbol
[440](https://docs.rs#440)            ));
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        }
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        std::fs::write(
[443](https://docs.rs#443)            out_dir.join("src").join("main.rs"),
[444](https://docs.rs#444)            format!("mod ffi_shims;\n{aliases}\n{rust_src}\n"),
[445](https://docs.rs#445)        )?;
[446](https://docs.rs#446)        Ok(())
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    }
[448](https://docs.rs#448)}
[449](https://docs.rs#449)
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// One emitted boundary's contribution to the shim file: an optional
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// `extern "C"` foreign declaration (C boundaries only), the safe wrapper, and
[452](https://docs.rs#452)/// the contract it cites (if a contract governs the strategy yet).
[453](https://docs.rs#453)struct ShimPart {
[454](https://docs.rs#454)    extern_decl: Option<String>,
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    wrapper: String,
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    contract: Option<&'static str>,
[457](https://docs.rs#457)}
[458](https://docs.rs#458)
[459](https://docs.rs#459)/// Exhaustive per-`to_lang` shim strategy. Every paradigm xpile knows is
[460](https://docs.rs#460)/// classified here — a real shim or a specific, mechanism-named gap — and a new
[461](https://docs.rs#461)/// [`SourceLang`] variant fails to compile until it is too (no wildcard arm).
[462](https://docs.rs#462)/// "Surface the gap" beats "mis-emit a wrong shim". Returns every failure reason
[463](https://docs.rs#463)/// for the boundary so the caller can report them all at once.
[464](https://docs.rs#464)fn shim_part_for(entry: &FfiEntry, modules: &[Module]) -> Result<ShimPart, Vec<String>> {
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    match entry.to_lang {
[466](https://docs.rs#466)        // Real, ABI-honest C-extension shim — the canonical CPython path.
[467](https://docs.rs#467)        SourceLang::C => match defining_function(modules, entry) {
[468](https://docs.rs#468)            Some(f) => emit_c_shim(entry, f),
[469](https://docs.rs#469)            None => Err(vec![format!(
[470](https://docs.rs#470)                "{}: resolved to a C symbol that is not a function (a const?) — \
[471](https://docs.rs#471)                 cannot emit a call shim",
[472](https://docs.rs#472)                entry.symbol
[473](https://docs.rs#473)            )]),
[474](https://docs.rs#474)        },
[475](https://docs.rs#475)        // Real subprocess shim — shell speaks argv + exit codes, which
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        // std::process::Command models exactly (no C ABI, no `unsafe`).
[477](https://docs.rs#477)        SourceLang::Shell => Ok(emit_shell_shim(entry)),
[478](https://docs.rs#478)        // Real pybind11 C++ shim (PMAT-927): a pybind11 extension exposes its
[479](https://docs.rs#479)        // C++ function to Python by a REGISTERED binding (`m.def("name", &fn)`),
[480](https://docs.rs#480)        // not as a flat C symbol — the underlying C++ symbol is name-mangled
[481](https://docs.rs#481)        // (`_Z...`), so a raw `extern "C"` of it would mis-link. The honest call
[482](https://docs.rs#482)        // path is the SAME one Python itself uses: embed CPython via pyo3, import
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        // the pybind11 module, and call the function by its Python-visible name.
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        // Like the C/pyo3 arms this needs the real defining function's signature.
[485](https://docs.rs#485)        SourceLang::Cpp => match (
[486](https://docs.rs#486)            defining_function(modules, entry),
[487](https://docs.rs#487)            defining_module_name(modules, entry),
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        ) {
[489](https://docs.rs#489)            (Some(f), Some(module_name)) => emit_pybind11_shim(entry, f, module_name),
[490](https://docs.rs#490)            _ => Err(vec![format!(
[491](https://docs.rs#491)                "{}: resolved to a C++ symbol that is not a function — cannot \
[492](https://docs.rs#492)                 emit a pybind11 shim",
[493](https://docs.rs#493)                entry.symbol
[494](https://docs.rs#494)            )]),
[495](https://docs.rs#495)        },
[496](https://docs.rs#496)        // Recognized boundary whose binding mechanism is not yet emitted. Names
[497](https://docs.rs#497)        // the real mechanism + roadmap phase so the gap is actionable.
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        SourceLang::Cuda => Err(vec![format!(
[499](https://docs.rs#499)            "{}: CUDA boundary → needs a host-launch shim (cudaLaunchKernel \
[500](https://docs.rs#500)             marshalling), not a direct call — roadmap Phase 7+",
[501](https://docs.rs#501)            entry.symbol
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        )]),
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        // Real pyo3 CPython-embedding shim (PMAT-926): a Rust/Ruchy driver
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        // calling a transpiled *Python* function embeds the interpreter via
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        // pyo3, imports the defining module, and calls the function under the
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        // GIL, marshalling args/return through pyo3's `IntoPyObject`/`extract`.
[507](https://docs.rs#507)        // Like the C arm this needs the real defining function's signature.
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        SourceLang::Python => match (
[509](https://docs.rs#509)            defining_function(modules, entry),
[510](https://docs.rs#510)            defining_module_name(modules, entry),
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        ) {
[512](https://docs.rs#512)            (Some(f), Some(module_name)) => emit_pyo3_shim(entry, f, module_name),
[513](https://docs.rs#513)            _ => Err(vec![format!(
[514](https://docs.rs#514)                "{}: resolved to a Python symbol that is not a function — cannot \
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                 emit a pyo3 embedding shim",
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                entry.symbol
[517](https://docs.rs#517)            )]),
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        },
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        // Real same-crate direct-call forwarder. Ruchy lowers to Rust and a Rust
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        // boundary is already Rust, so both land in the SAME emitted crate — a
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        // boundary call is a plain in-crate call, not FFI (no C ABI, no `unsafe`,
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        // no `extern` block). A missing defining function is the same internal
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        // invariant violation `reconcile` guards as for the C arm.
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        SourceLang::Ruchy | SourceLang::Rust => match defining_function(modules, entry) {
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            Some(f) => emit_direct_shim(entry, f),
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            None => Err(vec![format!(
[527](https://docs.rs#527)                "{}: resolved to a {:?} symbol that is not a function — cannot emit \
[528](https://docs.rs#528)                 a direct-call shim",
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                entry.symbol, entry.to_lang
[530](https://docs.rs#530)            )]),
[531](https://docs.rs#531)        },
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        SourceLang::Lean => Err(vec![format!(
[533](https://docs.rs#533)            "{}: Lean is the proof lane, not a runtime FFI target — a Lean boundary \
[534](https://docs.rs#534)             is a proof obligation, not a runtime shim",
[535](https://docs.rs#535)            entry.symbol
[536](https://docs.rs#536)        )]),
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        // Recognized boundary whose binding mechanism is not yet emitted. A
[538](https://docs.rs#538)        // transpiled WASM function isn't a flat C symbol — it lives inside a
[539](https://docs.rs#539)        // module that must be instantiated by a wasm runtime, and its exports
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        // are reached through typed-func marshalling, not a direct call. Names
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        // the real mechanism + roadmap slice so the gap is actionable (mirrors
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        // the Cuda host-launch arm).
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        SourceLang::Wasm => Err(vec![format!(
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            "{}: WASM boundary → needs a wasm-runtime host shim (wasmtime/wasmi \
[545](https://docs.rs#545)             module instantiation + typed-func marshalling), not a direct call — \
[546](https://docs.rs#546)             roadmap (bidirectional WASM, runtime stratum PMAT-952)",
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            entry.symbol
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        )]),
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    }
[550](https://docs.rs#550)}
[551](https://docs.rs#551)
[552](https://docs.rs#552)/// Emit a real C-extension shim: an `extern "C"` foreign declaration (symbol +
[553](https://docs.rs#553)/// ABI-honest arity) and a safe `*_shim` wrapper confining `unsafe`. Returns
[554](https://docs.rs#554)/// every ABI-mapping failure (each param + the return) so they can be reported
[555](https://docs.rs#555)/// together rather than one at a time.
[556](https://docs.rs#556)fn emit_c_shim(entry: &FfiEntry, f: &Function) -> Result<ShimPart, Vec<String>> {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    let mut unsupported = Vec::new();
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    let mut extern_params = Vec::new();
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    let mut wrap_params = Vec::new();
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    let mut call_args = Vec::new();
[561](https://docs.rs#561)    // PMAT-925: a `char*` param marshals through a `CString` that must outlive
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    // the FFI call (the C side borrows its buffer), so `let`-bind it BEFORE the
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    // `unsafe` call rather than building it inline as a temporary (whose buffer
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    // would be freed at the end of the call statement → dangling pointer).
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    let mut pre_call = Vec::new();
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    for p in &f.params {
[567](https://docs.rs#567)        // PMAT-924/925: `c_abi_render` covers scalars, raw pointers AND C
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        // strings; the `Marshal` strategy decides the wrapper's native type +
[569](https://docs.rs#569)        // how the argument crosses the boundary.
[570](https://docs.rs#570)        match c_abi_render(&p.ty) {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)            Some(abi) => {
[572](https://docs.rs#572)                extern_params.push(format!("{}: {}", p.name, abi.abi));
[573](https://docs.rs#573)                wrap_params.push(format!("{}: {}", p.name, abi.native_param));
[574](https://docs.rs#574)                match abi.marshal {
[575](https://docs.rs#575)                    // A scalar casts to its C ABI slot.
[576](https://docs.rs#576)                    Marshal::ScalarCast => {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)                        call_args.push(format!("{} as {}", p.name, abi.abi));
[578](https://docs.rs#578)                    }
[579](https://docs.rs#579)                    // A raw pointer is its own ABI form — pass straight through
[580](https://docs.rs#580)                    // (a self-cast would trip clippy::unnecessary_cast).
[581](https://docs.rs#581)                    Marshal::RawPtr => call_args.push(p.name.clone()),
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                    // PMAT-925: copy the `&str` into a NUL-terminated `CString`
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                    // (rejecting an interior NUL — the boundary cannot represent
[584](https://docs.rs#584)                    // it) and pass its borrowed pointer. The binding lives in the
[585](https://docs.rs#585)                    // wrapper's scope, so the buffer is valid for the whole call.
[586](https://docs.rs#586)                    Marshal::CStr => {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                        pre_call.push(format!(
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                            "    let __c_{0} = ::std::ffi::CString::new({0}).expect(\"interior NUL in `{0}` cannot cross the C-string boundary\");",
[589](https://docs.rs#589)                            p.name
[590](https://docs.rs#590)                        ));
[591](https://docs.rs#591)                        call_args.push(format!("__c_{}.as_ptr() as {}", p.name, abi.abi));
[592](https://docs.rs#592)                    }
[593](https://docs.rs#593)                }
[594](https://docs.rs#594)            }
[595](https://docs.rs#595)            None => unsupported.push(format!(
[596](https://docs.rs#596)                "{}: parameter `{}` type {:?} is not ABI-mappable to C",
[597](https://docs.rs#597)                entry.symbol, p.name, p.ty
[598](https://docs.rs#598)            )),
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        }
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    }
[601](https://docs.rs#601)
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    // Return position: Type::Unit is C `void` (no `-> T`); anything else must
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    // map, or the boundary is refused.
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    let (extern_ret, wrap_ret_sig, wrap_ret_expr) = match &f.return_type {
[605](https://docs.rs#605)        Type::Unit => (String::new(), String::new(), None),
[606](https://docs.rs#606)        ty => {
[607](https://docs.rs#607)            match c_abi_render(ty) {
[608](https://docs.rs#608)                Some(abi) => {
[609](https://docs.rs#609)                    let ret_expr = match abi.marshal {
[610](https://docs.rs#610)                    Marshal::ScalarCast => format!("__r as {}", abi.native_ret),
[611](https://docs.rs#611)                    // A raw pointer return needs no cast — `__r` is already the
[612](https://docs.rs#612)                    // native (= ABI) pointer type.
[613](https://docs.rs#613)                    Marshal::RawPtr => "__r".to_string(),
[614](https://docs.rs#614)                    // PMAT-925: the C side returns an owned `char*`; copy it into
[615](https://docs.rs#615)                    // a Rust `String` via a `CStr` view. `to_string_lossy` keeps
[616](https://docs.rs#616)                    // the shim total on non-UTF-8 bytes (the alternative — panic —
[617](https://docs.rs#617)                    // would violate the fail-closed posture). The raw pointer is
[618](https://docs.rs#618)                    // assumed non-null + NUL-terminated (the C contract); a null
[619](https://docs.rs#619)                    // would be UB, so this is the documented boundary obligation.
[620](https://docs.rs#620)                    Marshal::CStr => "unsafe { ::std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr(__r).to_string_lossy().into_owned() }".to_string(),
[621](https://docs.rs#621)                };
[622](https://docs.rs#622)                    (
[623](https://docs.rs#623)                        format!(" -> {}", abi.abi),
[624](https://docs.rs#624)                        format!(" -> {}", abi.native_ret),
[625](https://docs.rs#625)                        Some(ret_expr),
[626](https://docs.rs#626)                    )
[627](https://docs.rs#627)                }
[628](https://docs.rs#628)                None => {
[629](https://docs.rs#629)                    unsupported.push(format!(
[630](https://docs.rs#630)                        "{}: return type {:?} is not ABI-mappable to C",
[631](https://docs.rs#631)                        entry.symbol, ty
[632](https://docs.rs#632)                    ));
[633](https://docs.rs#633)                    (String::new(), String::new(), None)
[634](https://docs.rs#634)                }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)            }
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        }
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    };
[638](https://docs.rs#638)
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    if !unsupported.is_empty() {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        return Err(unsupported);
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    let extern_decl = format!(
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        "    // {}: {:?} -> {:?}\n    fn {}({}){};",
[645](https://docs.rs#645)        entry.shim_id,
[646](https://docs.rs#646)        entry.from_lang,
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        entry.to_lang,
[648](https://docs.rs#648)        entry.symbol,
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        extern_params.join(", "),
[650](https://docs.rs#650)        extern_ret
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    );
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    let call = format!("{}({})", entry.symbol, call_args.join(", "));
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    let pre = if pre_call.is_empty() {
[654](https://docs.rs#654)        String::new()
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    } else {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)        format!("{}\n", pre_call.join("\n"))
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    };
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    let body = match wrap_ret_expr {
[659](https://docs.rs#659)        Some(ret) => format!("{pre}    let __r = unsafe {{ {call} }};\n    {ret}\n"),
[660](https://docs.rs#660)        None => format!("{pre}    unsafe {{ {call} }}\n"),
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    };
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    let wrapper = format!(
[663](https://docs.rs#663)        "/// Safe wrapper for `{}` — confines `unsafe`; callers speak i64/f64/&str.\npub fn {}_shim({}){} {{\n{}}}\n",
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        entry.symbol,
[665](https://docs.rs#665)        entry.symbol,
[666](https://docs.rs#666)        wrap_params.join(", "),
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        wrap_ret_sig,
[668](https://docs.rs#668)        body
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    );
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    Ok(ShimPart {
[671](https://docs.rs#671)        extern_decl: Some(extern_decl),
[672](https://docs.rs#672)        wrapper,
[673](https://docs.rs#673)        contract: Some("C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT"),
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    })
[675](https://docs.rs#675)}
[676](https://docs.rs#676)
[677](https://docs.rs#677)/// Emit a real shell-subprocess shim. A shell boundary speaks argv strings + an
[678](https://docs.rs#678)/// exit code — exactly `std::process::Command`'s model — so the shim is a safe,
[679](https://docs.rs#679)/// `unsafe`-free wrapper that runs the transpiled POSIX symbol as a subprocess
[680](https://docs.rs#680)/// (the bashrs lane emits the script; this is the calling site that crosses into
[681](https://docs.rs#681)/// it). No `extern "C"` block: shell is not a C-ABI callee. Cites
[682](https://docs.rs#682)/// `C-FFI-SHELL-SUBPROCESS` (PMAT-907) — the argv-passthrough + exit-code-
[683](https://docs.rs#683)/// propagation contract governing this strategy, the calling-site companion of
[684](https://docs.rs#684)/// `C-BASHRS-POSIX-IDEMPOTENCE` (which governs the emitted shell *script*).
[685](https://docs.rs#685)fn emit_shell_shim(entry: &FfiEntry) -> ShimPart {
[686](https://docs.rs#686)    let wrapper = format!(
[687](https://docs.rs#687)        "/// Shell boundary `{0}` — runs the transpiled POSIX symbol as a subprocess.\n/// Shell speaks argv + exit codes, so the shim takes `&[&str]` args and returns\n/// the captured `Output` (no `unsafe`, no C ABI).\npub fn {0}_shim(args: &[&str]) -> ::std::io::Result<::std::process::Output> {{\n    ::std::process::Command::new(\"{0}\").args(args).output()\n}}\n",
[688](https://docs.rs#688)        entry.symbol
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    );
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    ShimPart {
[691](https://docs.rs#691)        extern_decl: None,
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        wrapper,
[693](https://docs.rs#693)        contract: Some("C-FFI-SHELL-SUBPROCESS"),
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    }
[695](https://docs.rs#695)}
[696](https://docs.rs#696)
[697](https://docs.rs#697)/// Emit a real **same-crate direct-call forwarder** for a Ruchy or Rust
[698](https://docs.rs#698)/// boundary. Ruchy lowers to Rust and a Rust boundary is already Rust, so both
[699](https://docs.rs#699)/// callees are native Rust functions in the SAME emitted crate — a boundary here
[700](https://docs.rs#700)/// is a plain in-crate call, not FFI. The shim is therefore a thin, safe wrapper
[701](https://docs.rs#701)/// that forwards to `symbol` with its native Rust signature: **no `extern "C"`
[702](https://docs.rs#702)/// block, no `unsafe`, no ABI marshalling** (contrast [`emit_c_shim`], which must
[703](https://docs.rs#703)/// cross the C ABI). Returns every non-native-mappable param/return reason
[704](https://docs.rs#704)/// together so the caller reports them all at once (mirrors [`emit_c_shim`]).
[705](https://docs.rs#705)/// Capability-ahead-of-contract — a direct call needs no FFI substrate, so
[706](https://docs.rs#706)/// `contract` is `None` (like the shell arm).
[707](https://docs.rs#707)fn emit_direct_shim(entry: &FfiEntry, f: &Function) -> Result<ShimPart, Vec<String>> {
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    let mut unsupported = Vec::new();
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    let mut params = Vec::new();
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    let mut args = Vec::new();
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    for p in &f.params {
[712](https://docs.rs#712)        match direct_native_type(&p.ty) {
[713](https://docs.rs#713)            Ok(rty) => {
[714](https://docs.rs#714)                params.push(format!("{}: {}", p.name, rty));
[715](https://docs.rs#715)                args.push(p.name.clone());
[716](https://docs.rs#716)            }
[717](https://docs.rs#717)            Err(reason) => {
[718](https://docs.rs#718)                unsupported.push(format!("{}: parameter `{}` {reason}", entry.symbol, p.name))
[719](https://docs.rs#719)            }
[720](https://docs.rs#720)        }
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    }
[722](https://docs.rs#722)
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    // Return position: `Type::Unit` is a bare `()` (no `-> T`), matching the rust
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    // backend; anything else must map to a native Rust type or the boundary is
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    // refused.
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    let ret_sig = match &f.return_type {
[727](https://docs.rs#727)        Type::Unit => String::new(),
[728](https://docs.rs#728)        ty => match direct_native_type(ty) {
[729](https://docs.rs#729)            Ok(rty) => format!(" -> {rty}"),
[730](https://docs.rs#730)            Err(reason) => {
[731](https://docs.rs#731)                unsupported.push(format!("{}: return type {reason}", entry.symbol));
[732](https://docs.rs#732)                String::new()
[733](https://docs.rs#733)            }
[734](https://docs.rs#734)        },
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    };
[736](https://docs.rs#736)
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    if !unsupported.is_empty() {
[738](https://docs.rs#738)        return Err(unsupported);
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    }
[740](https://docs.rs#740)
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    let wrapper = format!(
[742](https://docs.rs#742)        "/// Same-crate direct-call forwarder for `{0}` ({1:?} lowers to Rust — a\n\
[743](https://docs.rs#743)         /// boundary here is a plain in-crate call, not a foreign-function call).\n\
[744](https://docs.rs#744)         pub fn {0}_shim({2}){3} {{\n    {0}({4})\n}}\n",
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        entry.symbol,
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        entry.to_lang,
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        params.join(", "),
[748](https://docs.rs#748)        ret_sig,
[749](https://docs.rs#749)        args.join(", ")
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    );
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    Ok(ShimPart {
[752](https://docs.rs#752)        extern_decl: None,
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        wrapper,
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        contract: None,
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    })
[756](https://docs.rs#756)}
[757](https://docs.rs#757)
[758](https://docs.rs#758)/// PMAT-926: emit a real **pyo3 CPython-embedding shim** for a `to_lang ==
[759](https://docs.rs#759)/// Python` boundary. A Rust/Ruchy driver calling a transpiled *Python* function
[760](https://docs.rs#760)/// cannot lower it to native Rust (Python is dynamically typed — the only
[761](https://docs.rs#761)/// faithful execution is the CPython interpreter itself), so the shim EMBEDS
[762](https://docs.rs#762)/// CPython via pyo3: under the GIL it imports the defining module, fetches the
[763](https://docs.rs#763)/// function attribute, calls it with the marshalled args, and extracts the
[764](https://docs.rs#764)/// result back into the declared Rust scalar. This is the mechanism the prior
[765](https://docs.rs#765)/// `Err(pyo3 gap)` arm only named; it is now emitted.
[766](https://docs.rs#766)///
[767](https://docs.rs#767)/// Marshalling is restricted to the scalars pyo3 round-trips losslessly through
[768](https://docs.rs#768)/// its `IntoPyObject`/`FromPyObject` impls — `i64`/`f64`/`bool`/`String`. Any
[769](https://docs.rs#769)/// param/return whose meta-HIR type has no such pyo3 mapping (`List`/`Dict`/
[770](https://docs.rs#770)/// `BigInt`/`Struct`/a C-ABI width/…) is REFUSED with a named reason rather
[771](https://docs.rs#771)/// than mis-marshalled — the same refuse-rather-than-mis-emit posture as
[772](https://docs.rs#772)/// [`emit_c_shim`]. The module name is `entry.symbol`'s defining module; pyo3
[773](https://docs.rs#773)/// imports it by the function name's owning module, recorded on the boundary as
[774](https://docs.rs#774)/// the symbol's home. Capability-ahead-of-contract: a pyo3 embedding has no
[775](https://docs.rs#775)/// governing on-disk contract yet (a `C-FFI-PYO3-EMBED` is queued), so
[776](https://docs.rs#776)/// `contract` is `None` — exactly as the Ruchy/Rust direct-call arm shipped
[777](https://docs.rs#777)/// ahead of its contract.
[778](https://docs.rs#778)///
[779](https://docs.rs#779)/// No `extern "C"` block: pyo3 is a pure-Rust API over `libpython`, not a raw C
[780](https://docs.rs#780)/// ABI callee — the wrapper is `unsafe`-free (all `unsafe` lives inside pyo3).
[781](https://docs.rs#781)///
[782](https://docs.rs#782)/// `module_name` is the Python module that DEFINES the symbol (its `Module.name`
[783](https://docs.rs#783)/// in the dispatched set) — what pyo3's `PyModule::import` resolves; the shim
[784](https://docs.rs#784)/// `getattr`s `symbol` off it.
[785](https://docs.rs#785)fn emit_pyo3_shim(
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    entry: &FfiEntry,
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    f: &Function,
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    module_name: &str,
[789](https://docs.rs#789)) -> Result<ShimPart, Vec<String>> {
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    let mut unsupported = Vec::new();
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    let mut params = Vec::new();
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    // The call argument tuple. pyo3's `call1` takes a tuple; a 1-arg call needs
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    // the trailing comma (`(a,)`) to stay a tuple, and a 0-arg call passes the
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    // empty tuple `()`.
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    let mut call_args = Vec::new();
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    for p in &f.params {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)        match pyo3_native_type(&p.ty) {
[798](https://docs.rs#798)            Ok(rty) => {
[799](https://docs.rs#799)                params.push(format!("{}: {}", p.name, rty));
[800](https://docs.rs#800)                call_args.push(p.name.clone());
[801](https://docs.rs#801)            }
[802](https://docs.rs#802)            Err(reason) => {
[803](https://docs.rs#803)                unsupported.push(format!("{}: parameter `{}` {reason}", entry.symbol, p.name))
[804](https://docs.rs#804)            }
[805](https://docs.rs#805)        }
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    }
[807](https://docs.rs#807)
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    // Return position: `Type::Unit` is Python `None` (no `-> T`, no extract);
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    // anything else must map to a pyo3-extractable scalar or the boundary is
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    // refused.
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    let (ret_sig, extracts) = match &f.return_type {
[812](https://docs.rs#812)        Type::Unit => (String::new(), false),
[813](https://docs.rs#813)        ty => match pyo3_native_type(ty) {
[814](https://docs.rs#814)            Ok(rty) => (format!(" -> {rty}"), true),
[815](https://docs.rs#815)            Err(reason) => {
[816](https://docs.rs#816)                unsupported.push(format!("{}: return type {reason}", entry.symbol));
[817](https://docs.rs#817)                (String::new(), false)
[818](https://docs.rs#818)            }
[819](https://docs.rs#819)        },
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    };
[821](https://docs.rs#821)
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    if !unsupported.is_empty() {
[823](https://docs.rs#823)        return Err(unsupported);
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    }
[825](https://docs.rs#825)
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    let args_tuple = match call_args.len() {
[827](https://docs.rs#827)        0 => "()".to_string(),
[828](https://docs.rs#828)        1 => format!("({},)", call_args[0]),
[829](https://docs.rs#829)        _ => format!("({})", call_args.join(", ")),
[830](https://docs.rs#830)    };
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    let call_and_ret = if extracts {
[832](https://docs.rs#832)        format!(
[833](https://docs.rs#833)            "        let __r = __func\n            .call1({args_tuple})\n            .expect(\"call Python `{0}`\");\n        __r.extract().expect(\"extract `{0}` return into the declared Rust type\")\n",
[834](https://docs.rs#834)            entry.symbol
[835](https://docs.rs#835)        )
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    } else {
[837](https://docs.rs#837)        format!(
[838](https://docs.rs#838)            "        __func\n            .call1({args_tuple})\n            .expect(\"call Python `{0}`\");\n",
[839](https://docs.rs#839)            entry.symbol
[840](https://docs.rs#840)        )
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    };
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    let wrapper = format!(
[843](https://docs.rs#843)        "/// pyo3 CPython-embedding shim for `{0}` — embeds the interpreter, imports\n\
[844](https://docs.rs#844)         /// the transpiled Python module, and calls `{0}` under the GIL (no `unsafe`;\n\
[845](https://docs.rs#845)         /// all `unsafe` is confined inside pyo3). Callers speak native Rust scalars.\n\
[846](https://docs.rs#846)         pub fn {0}_shim({1}){2} {{\n\
[847](https://docs.rs#847)        \x20   // pyo3 0.23's `import`/`getattr`/`call1`/`extract` are trait methods\n\
[848](https://docs.rs#848)        \x20   // (`PyAnyMethods`/`PyModuleMethods`) — the prelude brings them in scope.\n\
[849](https://docs.rs#849)        \x20   // Function-local so it can't collide with sibling C/Shell/direct shims.\n\
[850](https://docs.rs#850)        \x20   use ::pyo3::prelude::*;\n\
[851](https://docs.rs#851)        \x20   ::pyo3::Python::with_gil(|py| {{\n\
[852](https://docs.rs#852)        \x20       let __module = ::pyo3::types::PyModule::import(py, \"{3}\")\n\
[853](https://docs.rs#853)        \x20           .expect(\"import the transpiled Python module `{3}`\");\n\
[854](https://docs.rs#854)        \x20       let __func = __module\n\
[855](https://docs.rs#855)        \x20           .getattr(\"{0}\")\n\
[856](https://docs.rs#856)        \x20           .expect(\"Python module `{3}` defines `{0}`\");\n\
[857](https://docs.rs#857)        {4}\
[858](https://docs.rs#858)        \x20   }})\n\
[859](https://docs.rs#859)         }}\n",
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        entry.symbol,
[861](https://docs.rs#861)        params.join(", "),
[862](https://docs.rs#862)        ret_sig,
[863](https://docs.rs#863)        module_name,
[864](https://docs.rs#864)        call_and_ret
[865](https://docs.rs#865)    );
[866](https://docs.rs#866)    Ok(ShimPart {
[867](https://docs.rs#867)        extern_decl: None,
[868](https://docs.rs#868)        wrapper,
[869](https://docs.rs#869)        // Capability-ahead-of-contract: a pyo3 embedding has no on-disk contract
[870](https://docs.rs#870)        // yet (a C-FFI-PYO3-EMBED is queued) — same posture as the direct-call arm.
[871](https://docs.rs#871)        contract: None,
[872](https://docs.rs#872)    })
[873](https://docs.rs#873)}
[874](https://docs.rs#874)
[875](https://docs.rs#875)/// PMAT-926: the native Rust type a **pyo3 embedding shim** speaks for a
[876](https://docs.rs#876)/// meta-HIR [`Type`]. The accepted set is the scalars pyo3 round-trips
[877](https://docs.rs#877)/// losslessly through its `IntoPyObject`/`FromPyObject` blanket impls: a Python
[878](https://docs.rs#878)/// `int` is `i64`, a `float` is `f64`, a `bool` is `bool`, a `str` is owned
[879](https://docs.rs#879)/// `String`. Everything else is REFUSED with a named reason (the
[880](https://docs.rs#880)/// refuse-rather-than-mis-marshal posture): a C-ABI integer/float WIDTH
[881](https://docs.rs#881)/// (`CLong`/`CUInt`/`CULong`/`F32`) is a C-sourced shape that has no business at
[882](https://docs.rs#882)/// a Python boundary; `BigInt` needs a `num-bigint`↔pyo3 bridge the first cut
[883](https://docs.rs#883)/// does not pin; containers (`List`/`Dict`/`Set`/`Tuple`/`Optional`) and a
[884](https://docs.rs#884)/// `Struct` need a recursive pyo3 marshalling pass (deferred); a raw pointer /
[885](https://docs.rs#885)/// `CChar` is a C-ABI token, not a Python value; the bashrs-domain types and a
[886](https://docs.rs#886)/// bare `Unit` parameter are nonsensical at this boundary.
[887](https://docs.rs#887)fn pyo3_native_type(ty: &Type) -> Result<String, String> {
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    Ok(match ty {
[889](https://docs.rs#889)        Type::I64 => "i64".to_string(),
[890](https://docs.rs#890)        Type::F64 => "f64".to_string(),
[891](https://docs.rs#891)        Type::Bool => "bool".to_string(),
[892](https://docs.rs#892)        Type::Str => "String".to_string(),
[893](https://docs.rs#893)        Type::CLong | Type::CUInt | Type::CULong | Type::F32 => {
[894](https://docs.rs#894)            return Err(format!(
[895](https://docs.rs#895)                "type {ty:?} is a C-ABI width — a C-sourced shape with no place at a \
[896](https://docs.rs#896)                 Python (pyo3) boundary; pyo3 marshals plain Python int/float"
[897](https://docs.rs#897)            ));
[898](https://docs.rs#898)        }
[899](https://docs.rs#899)        Type::BigInt => {
[900](https://docs.rs#900)            return Err(
[901](https://docs.rs#901)                "type BigInt needs a num-bigint↔pyo3 bridge the embedding shim does \
[902](https://docs.rs#902)                 not pin; pyo3 shim refuses it"
[903](https://docs.rs#903)                    .to_string(),
[904](https://docs.rs#904)            );
[905](https://docs.rs#905)        }
[906](https://docs.rs#906)        Type::List(_) | Type::Dict(_, _) | Type::Set(_) | Type::Tuple(_) | Type::Optional(_) => {
[907](https://docs.rs#907)            return Err(format!(
[908](https://docs.rs#908)                "container type {ty:?} needs a recursive pyo3 marshalling pass — \
[909](https://docs.rs#909)                 the embedding shim's first cut speaks scalars only; refused"
[910](https://docs.rs#910)            ));
[911](https://docs.rs#911)        }
[912](https://docs.rs#912)        Type::Struct(name) => {
[913](https://docs.rs#913)            return Err(format!(
[914](https://docs.rs#914)                "struct type `{name}` needs a co-emitted `#[pyclass]` bridge — \
[915](https://docs.rs#915)                 pyo3 shim refuses it until struct marshalling lands"
[916](https://docs.rs#916)            ));
[917](https://docs.rs#917)        }
[918](https://docs.rs#918)        Type::Ptr { .. } | Type::CChar => {
[919](https://docs.rs#919)            return Err(format!(
[920](https://docs.rs#920)                "type {ty:?} is a C-ABI pointer/char token, not a Python value — \
[921](https://docs.rs#921)                 pyo3 shim refuses it"
[922](https://docs.rs#922)            ));
[923](https://docs.rs#923)        }
[924](https://docs.rs#924)        Type::ShellString | Type::ExitCode => {
[925](https://docs.rs#925)            return Err(format!(
[926](https://docs.rs#926)                "type {ty:?} is a bashrs-domain type — not a pyo3 marshalling target"
[927](https://docs.rs#927)            ));
[928](https://docs.rs#928)        }
[929](https://docs.rs#929)        Type::Unit => {
[930](https://docs.rs#930)            return Err("type `()` is only valid in return position".to_string());
[931](https://docs.rs#931)        }
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    })
[933](https://docs.rs#933)}
[934](https://docs.rs#934)
[935](https://docs.rs#935)/// PMAT-927: emit a real **pybind11 C++ shim** for a `to_lang == Cpp` boundary.
[936](https://docs.rs#936)///
[937](https://docs.rs#937)/// Name-mangling reality, handled honestly. A pybind11 extension does NOT export
[938](https://docs.rs#938)/// its C++ function as a flat C symbol: the C++ symbol is name-mangled by the
[939](https://docs.rs#939)/// Itanium ABI (`_Z<len><name>...` — `&square_sum` becomes `_Z10square_sumi`),
[940](https://docs.rs#940)/// so a raw `extern "C" { fn square_sum(...) }` would fail to link against the
[941](https://docs.rs#941)/// real `.so`. What pybind11 publishes instead is a Python-callable *binding*
[942](https://docs.rs#942)/// registered at module-init (`m.def("square_sum", &square_sum)`), keyed by the
[943](https://docs.rs#943)/// Python-VISIBLE name (the string literal), not the mangled symbol. The only
[944](https://docs.rs#944)/// link-honest way to invoke it is the SAME path Python uses: go through the
[945](https://docs.rs#945)/// registered binding. So this shim EMBEDS CPython via pyo3 (a pybind11 module
[946](https://docs.rs#946)/// IS a CPython extension module), imports it, and calls the function by its
[947](https://docs.rs#947)/// Python name — refusing rather than mis-emitting a guessed mangled `extern`.
[948](https://docs.rs#948)///
[949](https://docs.rs#949)/// This is mechanically the pyo3-embedding path ([`emit_pyo3_shim`]) — the
[950](https://docs.rs#950)/// difference is the boundary's PROVENANCE (a C++ pybind11 `.so`, not a `.py`),
[951](https://docs.rs#951)/// recorded in the doc comment and the marshalling rules: pybind11's automatic
[952](https://docs.rs#952)/// type casters round-trip Python `int`/`float`/`bool`/`str` to C++
[953](https://docs.rs#953)/// `long`/`double`/`bool`/`std::string`, so the accepted Rust scalar set is the
[954](https://docs.rs#954)/// same `i64`/`f64`/`bool`/`String` ([`pybind11_native_type`]). Any type
[955](https://docs.rs#955)/// pybind11's *automatic* casters don't carry losslessly (a C-ABI width, a
[956](https://docs.rs#956)/// container needing `pybind11/stl.h`, a `BigInt`, a struct needing
[957](https://docs.rs#957)/// `py::class_`) is REFUSED with a named reason rather than mis-marshalled.
[958](https://docs.rs#958)///
[959](https://docs.rs#959)/// No `extern "C"` block, no `unsafe` in the emitted wrapper: all the `unsafe`
[960](https://docs.rs#960)/// lives inside pyo3. Capability-ahead-of-contract: a pybind11 embedding has no
[961](https://docs.rs#961)/// governing on-disk contract yet (a `C-FFI-PYBIND11-EMBED` is queued), so
[962](https://docs.rs#962)/// `contract` is `None` — exactly as the pyo3 and direct-call arms shipped ahead
[963](https://docs.rs#963)/// of theirs. `module_name` is the pybind11 module that registers the binding
[964](https://docs.rs#964)/// (its `Module.name` in the dispatched set) — what `PyModule::import` resolves.
[965](https://docs.rs#965)fn emit_pybind11_shim(
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    entry: &FfiEntry,
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    f: &Function,
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    module_name: &str,
[969](https://docs.rs#969)) -> Result<ShimPart, Vec<String>> {
[970](https://docs.rs#970)    let mut unsupported = Vec::new();
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    let mut params = Vec::new();
[972](https://docs.rs#972)    // pybind11's bound function is invoked through pyo3's `call1`, which takes a
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    // tuple: a 1-arg call needs the trailing comma (`(a,)`) to stay a tuple; a
[974](https://docs.rs#974)    // 0-arg call passes the empty tuple `()`.
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    let mut call_args = Vec::new();
[976](https://docs.rs#976)    for p in &f.params {
