[977](https://docs.rs#977)        match pybind11_native_type(&p.ty) {
[978](https://docs.rs#978)            Ok(rty) => {
[979](https://docs.rs#979)                params.push(format!("{}: {}", p.name, rty));
[980](https://docs.rs#980)                call_args.push(p.name.clone());
[981](https://docs.rs#981)            }
[982](https://docs.rs#982)            Err(reason) => {
[983](https://docs.rs#983)                unsupported.push(format!("{}: parameter `{}` {reason}", entry.symbol, p.name))
[984](https://docs.rs#984)            }
[985](https://docs.rs#985)        }
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    }
[987](https://docs.rs#987)
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    // Return position: `Type::Unit` is C++ `void` / Python `None` (no `-> T`, no
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    // extract); anything else must map to a pybind11-castable scalar or refuse.
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    let (ret_sig, extracts) = match &f.return_type {
[991](https://docs.rs#991)        Type::Unit => (String::new(), false),
[992](https://docs.rs#992)        ty => match pybind11_native_type(ty) {
[993](https://docs.rs#993)            Ok(rty) => (format!(" -> {rty}"), true),
[994](https://docs.rs#994)            Err(reason) => {
[995](https://docs.rs#995)                unsupported.push(format!("{}: return type {reason}", entry.symbol));
[996](https://docs.rs#996)                (String::new(), false)
[997](https://docs.rs#997)            }
[998](https://docs.rs#998)        },
[999](https://docs.rs#999)    };
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)    if !unsupported.is_empty() {
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)        return Err(unsupported);
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)    }
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)    let args_tuple = match call_args.len() {
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)        0 => "()".to_string(),
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)        1 => format!("({},)", call_args[0]),
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)        _ => format!("({})", call_args.join(", ")),
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)    };
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)    let call_and_ret = if extracts {
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)        format!(
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)            "        let __r = __func\n            .call1({args_tuple})\n            .expect(\"call pybind11-bound `{0}`\");\n        __r.extract().expect(\"extract `{0}` return into the declared Rust type\")\n",
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)            entry.symbol
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)        )
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)    } else {
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)        format!(
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)            "        __func\n            .call1({args_tuple})\n            .expect(\"call pybind11-bound `{0}`\");\n",
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)            entry.symbol
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)        )
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)    };
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)    let wrapper = format!(
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)        "/// pybind11 C++ shim for `{0}` — the C++ symbol is name-mangled, so this\n\
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)         /// calls the pybind11-registered binding (`m.def(\"{0}\", ...)`) by its\n\
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)         /// Python-visible name through the embedded interpreter, NOT a guessed\n\
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)         /// `extern \"C\"` (which would mis-link). No `unsafe` (it is confined inside\n\
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)         /// pyo3); callers speak native Rust scalars.\n\
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)         pub fn {0}_shim({1}){2} {{\n\
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)        \x20   // A pybind11 extension IS a CPython extension module; pyo3 imports it\n\
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)        \x20   // and `call1`s the bound function exactly as the Python interpreter would.\n\
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        \x20   use ::pyo3::prelude::*;\n\
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)        \x20   ::pyo3::Python::with_gil(|py| {{\n\
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)        \x20       let __module = ::pyo3::types::PyModule::import(py, \"{3}\")\n\
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)        \x20           .expect(\"import the pybind11 extension module `{3}`\");\n\
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)        \x20       let __func = __module\n\
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)        \x20           .getattr(\"{0}\")\n\
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)        \x20           .expect(\"pybind11 module `{3}` binds `{0}`\");\n\
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)        {4}\
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)        \x20   }})\n\
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)         }}\n",
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)        entry.symbol,
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)        params.join(", "),
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)        ret_sig,
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)        module_name,
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)        call_and_ret
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)    );
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)    Ok(ShimPart {
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)        extern_decl: None,
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)        wrapper,
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)        // Capability-ahead-of-contract: a pybind11 embedding has no on-disk
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)        // contract yet (a C-FFI-PYBIND11-EMBED is queued) — same posture as the
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)        // pyo3 and direct-call arms.
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)        contract: None,
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)    })
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)}
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)/// PMAT-927: the native Rust type a **pybind11 C++ shim** speaks for a meta-HIR
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)/// [`Type`]. The accepted set is the scalars pybind11's AUTOMATIC type casters
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)/// round-trip through the embedded interpreter without an extra header/binding:
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)/// a C++ `long`/`int` is Python `int` is Rust `i64`, a `double`/`float` is
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)/// Python `float` is `f64`, a `bool` is `bool`, a `std::string`/`const char*` is
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)/// Python `str` is owned `String`. Everything else is REFUSED with a named
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)/// reason (the refuse-rather-than-mis-emit posture): a C-ABI integer/float WIDTH
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)/// (`CLong`/`CUInt`/`CULong`/`F32`) is a decy C-sourced shape, not a pybind11
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)/// boundary token (pybind11 carries plain Python int/float); `BigInt` needs a
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)/// `py::int_`↔num-bigint bridge the first cut does not pin; a container
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)/// (`List`/`Dict`/`Set`/`Tuple`/`Optional`) needs `#include <pybind11/stl.h>`
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)/// PLUS a recursive marshalling pass (deferred); a `Struct` needs a co-emitted
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)/// `py::class_<T>` binding; a raw pointer / `CChar` is a flat-C-ABI token, not a
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)/// pybind11 value; the bashrs-domain types and a bare `Unit` parameter are
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)/// nonsensical at this boundary.
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)fn pybind11_native_type(ty: &Type) -> Result<String, String> {
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)    Ok(match ty {
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)        Type::I64 => "i64".to_string(),
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)        Type::F64 => "f64".to_string(),
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)        Type::Bool => "bool".to_string(),
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)        Type::Str => "String".to_string(),
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)        Type::CLong | Type::CUInt | Type::CULong | Type::F32 => {
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)            return Err(format!(
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)                "type {ty:?} is a C-ABI width — a decy C-sourced shape with no place \
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)                 at a pybind11 boundary; pybind11 carries plain Python int/float"
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)            ));
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)        }
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)        Type::BigInt => {
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)            return Err(
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)                "type BigInt needs a py::int_↔num-bigint bridge the pybind11 shim \
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)                 does not pin; pybind11 shim refuses it"
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)                    .to_string(),
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)            );
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)        }
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)        Type::List(_) | Type::Dict(_, _) | Type::Set(_) | Type::Tuple(_) | Type::Optional(_) => {
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)            return Err(format!(
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)                "container type {ty:?} needs `#include <pybind11/stl.h>` plus a \
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)                 recursive marshalling pass — the pybind11 shim's first cut speaks \
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)                 scalars only; refused"
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)            ));
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)        }
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)        Type::Struct(name) => {
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)            return Err(format!(
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)                "struct type `{name}` needs a co-emitted `py::class_<{name}>` binding \
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)                 — pybind11 shim refuses it until struct marshalling lands"
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)            ));
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)        }
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)        Type::Ptr { .. } | Type::CChar => {
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)            return Err(format!(
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)                "type {ty:?} is a flat-C-ABI pointer/char token, not a pybind11 value \
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)                 — pybind11 shim refuses it"
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)            ));
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)        }
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)        Type::ShellString | Type::ExitCode => {
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)            return Err(format!(
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)                "type {ty:?} is a bashrs-domain type — not a pybind11 marshalling target"
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)            ));
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)        }
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)        Type::Unit => {
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)            return Err("type `()` is only valid in return position".to_string());
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)        }
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)    })
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)}
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)/// Native Rust type a **same-crate direct-call** shim speaks for a meta-HIR
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)/// [`Type`]. Unlike [`c_abi_type`] there is NO C ABI to honor (the callee is
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)/// native Rust in the same crate), so the accepted set is wider — it mirrors what
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)/// `xpile-rust-codegen` emits for a signature, but only for the **dependency-free
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)/// std** types, because the emitted hybrid workspace pins `[dependencies]` empty.
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)/// Types whose Rust lowering needs an external crate (`BigInt` →
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)/// `xpile_bigint`, `Dict` → `indexmap`) or a co-emitted definition (`Struct`) are
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)/// refused with a named reason rather than emitting an unbuildable forwarder; the
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)/// bashrs-domain types are refused as the rust backend refuses them. A `Unit`
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)/// parameter is nonsensical (Unit is a return-only shape, handled by the caller).
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)fn direct_native_type(ty: &Type) -> Result<String, String> {
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)    Ok(match ty {
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)        Type::I64 => "i64".to_string(),
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)        // PMAT-909: a C `long`/`int64_t` is value-compatible with I64 in a
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)        // native (no-C-ABI) direct call — both speak `i64`.
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)        Type::CLong => "i64".to_string(),
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)        // PMAT-918: a C `unsigned`/`uint32_t` direct-call shim speaks native
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)        // `u32` — the signedness is preserved even off the C ABI.
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)        Type::CUInt => "u32".to_string(),
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)        // PMAT-921: a C `unsigned long`/`uint64_t` direct-call shim speaks
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)        // native `u64` — both 64-bit width and signedness preserved off the ABI.
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)        Type::CULong => "u64".to_string(),
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)        Type::F64 => "f64".to_string(),
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)        // PMAT-911: a C `float` direct-call shim speaks native `f32`.
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)        Type::F32 => "f32".to_string(),
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)        Type::Bool => "bool".to_string(),
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)        Type::Str => "String".to_string(),
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)        Type::List(elem) => format!("Vec<{}>", direct_native_type(elem)?),
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)        Type::Set(elem) => format!("std::collections::HashSet<{}>", direct_native_type(elem)?),
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)        Type::Optional(inner) => format!("Option<{}>", direct_native_type(inner)?),
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        Type::Tuple(elems) => {
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)            let mut parts = Vec::with_capacity(elems.len());
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)            for e in elems {
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)                parts.push(direct_native_type(e)?);
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)            }
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)            // A 1-tuple needs the trailing comma — `(T,)` — to stay a tuple.
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)            if parts.len() == 1 {
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)                format!("({},)", parts[0])
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)            } else {
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)                format!("({})", parts.join(", "))
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)            }
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)        }
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)        Type::Unit => {
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)            return Err("type `()` is only valid in return position".to_string());
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)        }
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)        Type::BigInt => {
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)            return Err(
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)                "type BigInt lowers to xpile_bigint::BigInt — a non-std dep the \
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)                        hybrid workspace does not pin; direct-call shim refuses it"
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)                    .to_string(),
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)            );
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)        }
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)        Type::Dict(_, _) => {
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)            return Err(
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)                "type Dict lowers to indexmap::IndexMap — a non-std dep the \
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)                        hybrid workspace does not pin; direct-call shim refuses it"
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)                    .to_string(),
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)            );
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)        }
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)        Type::Struct(name) => {
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)            return Err(format!(
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)                "struct type `{name}` needs its definition co-emitted into the shim crate \
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)                 — direct-call shim refuses it until struct re-export lands"
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)            ));
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)        }
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)        Type::ShellString | Type::ExitCode => {
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)            return Err(format!(
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)                "type {ty:?} is a bashrs-domain type (contract C-BASHRS-POSIX-IDEMPOTENCE) \
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)                 — not a direct-call shim target"
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)            ));
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)        }
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)        // PMAT-924: a raw C pointer in a same-crate direct call renders as a raw
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)        // Rust pointer `*mut`/`*const <native-pointee>` — sound to DECLARE in a
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)        // forwarder signature (only a deref would be `unsafe`). The pointee must
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)        // itself be a native-mappable scalar; a `char` pointee (`CChar`) becomes
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)        // `*mut i8` (the platform-honest `c_char` already lives on the C-ABI
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)        // path; in a NATIVE direct call there is no C ABI, so `CChar` is the
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)        // `i8` byte). A bare `CChar` (non-pointer) is refused.
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)        Type::Ptr { mutable, pointee } => {
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)            let inner = direct_native_type(pointee)?;
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)            let qualifier = if *mutable { "mut" } else { "const" };
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)            format!("*{qualifier} {inner}")
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)        }
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)        Type::CChar => "i8".to_string(),
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)    })
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)}
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)/// Recover the real defining [`Function`] for a reconciled entry, mirroring
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)/// [`FfiManifest::reconcile`]'s symbol/`to_lang` match. `reconcile` guarantees an
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)/// entry exists only when the symbol is defined, so a miss here is an internal
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)/// invariant violation (surfaced as an unsupported boundary by the caller).
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)/// The defining function for a reconciled boundary: the `Item::Function` named
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)/// `entry.symbol` in the module whose `source_lang` is `entry.to_lang`. Public so
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)/// the `--verify` flow (PMAT-902) can read the C callee's param/return types to
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)/// build the CPython-side ctypes ABI binding for the differential reference.
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)pub fn defining_function<'a>(modules: &'a [Module], entry: &FfiEntry) -> Option<&'a Function> {
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)    for m in modules {
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)        if m.source_lang != entry.to_lang {
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)            continue;
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)        }
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)        for it in &m.items {
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)            if let Item::Function(f) = it {
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)                if f.name == entry.symbol {
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)                    return Some(f);
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)                }
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)            }
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)        }
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)    }
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)    None
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)}
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)/// PMAT-931 (HUNT correctness — the PMAT-930 `c_double` two-arg divergence):
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)/// after reconciliation, re-type the FFI call sites of every reconciled symbol
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)/// whose `to_lang` definition returns `Type::F64` so the float-repr path is
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)/// selected in the calling (Python) module.
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)///
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)/// The Python frontend lowers `app.py` BEFORE the C sibling is dispatched, so a
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)/// call to a `double`-returning C symbol is typed with the unknown-callee I64
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)/// default. That makes `print(scale2(...))` print a whole double as `10` (not
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)/// Python's `10.0`) and `let r: float = scale2(...)` emit `let r: i64` (rustc
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)/// E0308). This walks each non-`to_lang` module and corrects those sites via
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)/// [`xpile_meta_hir::retype_ffi_float_call_sites`]. Idempotent / no-op when no
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)/// reconciled symbol returns F64.
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)pub fn retype_float_ffi_sites(manifest: &FfiManifest, modules: &mut [Module]) {
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)    // The set of reconciled FFI symbols whose defining (to_lang) function
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)    // returns F64 — these are the call sites the calling module mistyped.
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)    let float_symbols: std::collections::HashSet<String> = manifest
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)        .entries
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)        .iter()
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)        .filter(|e| defining_function(modules, e).is_some_and(|f| f.return_type == Type::F64))
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)        .map(|e| e.symbol.clone())
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)        .collect();
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    if float_symbols.is_empty() {
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)        return;
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    }
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)    for m in modules.iter_mut() {
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)        // Only the calling-side modules need correction; a defining `to_lang`
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)        // (C) module has no Python print/let sites and is skipped by the emit
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)        // path anyway.
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)        if matches!(
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)            m.source_lang,
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)            SourceLang::C | SourceLang::Cpp | SourceLang::Cuda
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)        ) {
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)            continue;
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)        }
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)        xpile_meta_hir::retype_ffi_float_call_sites(m, &float_symbols);
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)    }
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)}
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)/// PMAT-926: the NAME of the module that defines a reconciled entry's symbol —
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)/// what pyo3's `PyModule::import` resolves for a Python-embedding shim. Mirrors
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)/// [`defining_function`]'s symbol/`to_lang` match. Returns `None` when no module
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)/// defines the symbol — an internal-invariant violation `reconcile` already
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)/// guards (the caller only reaches the pyo3 arm after `defining_function`
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)/// succeeded), so in practice this is always `Some`.
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)fn defining_module_name<'a>(modules: &'a [Module], entry: &FfiEntry) -> Option<&'a str> {
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)    for m in modules {
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)        if m.source_lang != entry.to_lang {
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)            continue;
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)        }
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)        for it in &m.items {
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)            if let Item::Function(f) = it {
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)                if f.name == entry.symbol {
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)                    return Some(&m.name);
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)                }
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)            }
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)        }
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)    }
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)    None
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)}
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)/// ABI-honest meta-HIR `Type` → Rust FFI type for a `to_lang == C` boundary.
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)/// Returns `None` for types the first cut refuses (pointer/string/container/
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)/// struct) rather than mis-marshal.
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)///
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)/// DECY-FIDELITY CEILING (PMAT-909/910 partial lift): decy models C `int` (a
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)/// 32-bit type) as `Type::I64`, so `I64 → c_int` keeps that boundary
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)/// 32-bit-honest. A genuine C `long`/`int64_t` now parses to the DISTINCT
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)/// `Type::CLong` width (decy-frontend, PMAT-909) and maps to `c_longlong` —
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)/// no longer narrowed to `c_int`. C `double` parses to `Type::F64` and maps
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)/// to `c_double` (PMAT-910), the FFI boundary having been F64-ready ahead of
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)/// the decy lexer. C `float` now parses to the DISTINCT `Type::F32` width
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)/// (decy-frontend, PMAT-911) and maps to `c_float` (a 32-bit ABI slot) — never
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)/// widened through `c_double`. C `unsigned`/`unsigned int`/`uint32_t` now parses
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)/// to the DISTINCT `Type::CUInt` width (decy-frontend, PMAT-918) and maps to the
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)/// UNSIGNED `c_uint` slot — never the signed `c_int`. C `unsigned long`/`unsigned
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)/// long long`/`uint64_t` now parses to the DISTINCT `Type::CULong` width
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)/// (decy-frontend, PMAT-921) and maps to the UNSIGNED 64-bit `c_ulonglong` slot —
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)/// never the 32-bit `c_uint` (truncation) nor the signed `c_longlong`. A C
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)/// pointer `T*` now parses to the DISTINCT `Type::Ptr` (decy-frontend, PMAT-924)
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)/// — the first address-carrying ABI token — and `c_abi_render` (NOT this
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)/// `&'static str` function, which can't express a formatted `*mut <abi>`) maps
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)/// it to a raw `*mut`/`*const <pointee-ABI>`; an 8-bit `char` pointee maps to
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)/// the `c_char` slot here. PMAT-925 closes the last ceiling: a `char*` is now
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)/// MARSHALLED to/from a Rust `&str`/`String` (a `CString`/`CStr` round-trip) by
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)/// `c_abi_render`/`emit_c_shim` rather than leaking the raw `*mut c_char`.
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)/// `Bool → c_int` is a lossy forward guard (decy never produces `Bool`);
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)/// `Type::Unit` is handled at the return position; `Type::Ptr` is `None` here
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)/// (handled by `c_abi_render`).
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)fn c_abi_type(ty: &Type) -> Option<&'static str> {
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    match ty {
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)        Type::I64 | Type::Bool => Some("::std::os::raw::c_int"),
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)        // PMAT-909: a 64-bit C integer rides the `long long` ABI slot
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)        // (always ≥64-bit, unlike platform-variable `long`) — never
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)        // narrowed to `c_int`.
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)        Type::CLong => Some("::std::os::raw::c_longlong"),
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)        // PMAT-918: a 32-bit UNSIGNED C int rides the DISTINCT `c_uint` ABI
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)        // slot — never the signed `c_int` (a value ≥ 2³¹ would otherwise be
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)        // reinterpreted as negative at the boundary).
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)        Type::CUInt => Some("::std::os::raw::c_uint"),
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)        // PMAT-921: a 64-bit UNSIGNED C int rides the DISTINCT `c_ulonglong`
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)        // ABI slot — never the 32-bit `c_uint` (which would truncate a value
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)        // ≥ 2³²) nor the signed `c_longlong` (which would reinterpret a value
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)        // ≥ 2⁶³ as negative).
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)        Type::CULong => Some("::std::os::raw::c_ulonglong"),
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)        Type::F64 => Some("::std::os::raw::c_double"),
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)        // PMAT-911: a 32-bit C float rides the DISTINCT `c_float` ABI slot —
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)        // never widened through `c_double` (the 32↔64 ABI honesty held for
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)        // floats as PMAT-909 held it for ints).
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)        Type::F32 => Some("::std::os::raw::c_float"),
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)        // PMAT-924: an 8-bit C `char` rides the platform-signedness-honest
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)        // `c_char` ABI slot. It reaches a boundary ONLY as a pointer pointee
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)        // (`char*` -> `*mut c_char`); a bare `char` value never appears (decy
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)        // refuses it). The pointer wrapping is handled by `c_abi_render`.
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)        Type::CChar => Some("::std::os::raw::c_char"),
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)        _ => None,
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)    }
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)}
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)/// The native Rust type the safe wrapper speaks for an ABI-mappable `Type`
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)/// (callers use i64/f64; the wrapper casts to/from the C ABI type internally).
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)fn wrapper_native(ty: &Type) -> &'static str {
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)    match ty {
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)        Type::F64 => "f64",
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)        // PMAT-911: a C `float` wrapper speaks `f32` (casts to/from `c_float`).
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)        Type::F32 => "f32",
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)        // PMAT-918: a C `unsigned`/`uint32_t` wrapper speaks `u32` (casts
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)        // to/from `c_uint`) — the signedness MUST survive the wrapper, so this
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)        // cannot fall through to the `i64` default below.
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)        Type::CUInt => "u32",
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)        // PMAT-921: a C `unsigned long`/`uint64_t` wrapper speaks `u64` (casts
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)        // to/from `c_ulonglong`) — both 64-bit width and signedness MUST survive
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)        // the wrapper, so this cannot fall through to the `i64` default below.
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)        Type::CULong => "u64",
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)        // I64, the Bool forward-guard, and the PMAT-909 CLong all ride an
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)        // `i64` native wrapper (CLong casts to/from `c_longlong`; I64 to/from
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)        // `c_int`).
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)        _ => "i64",
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)    }
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)}
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)/// How the safe wrapper bridges its native type to/from the C ABI slot.
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)enum Marshal {
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)    /// A scalar `i64`/`f64`/`u32`/… that casts to/from its `c_int`/`c_double`/…
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    /// ABI slot with a plain `as` (PMAT-909/911/918/921).
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    ScalarCast,
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    /// A raw `*mut`/`*const <scalar>` whose native form IS its ABI form, so no
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)    /// cast and no marshalling — the wrapper passes the pointer straight through
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)    /// (PMAT-924, a non-`char` pointee like `int*`/`double*`).
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)    RawPtr,
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)    /// PMAT-925: a C string (`char*`) marshalled to/from an owned Rust
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)    /// `String` (return) or borrowed `&str` (param) via a `CString`/`CStr`
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)    /// round-trip — the LAST decy ABI ceiling. The wrapper speaks `&str`/
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)    /// `String`, never the raw `*mut c_char`, so `unsafe` raw-pointer handling
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)    /// is confined to the shim.
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)    CStr,
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)}
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)/// PMAT-924/925: the ABI-honest rendering of a meta-HIR [`Type`] at a C boundary —
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)/// the `extern "C"` ABI type, the native type the safe wrapper speaks, and HOW the
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)/// wrapper bridges between them ([`Marshal`]). A SCALAR delegates to
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)/// [`c_abi_type`]/[`wrapper_native`] (caller speaks i64/f64, so a cast to/from the
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)/// c_int/c_double ABI slot is required: `Marshal::ScalarCast`). A POINTER
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)/// ([`Type::Ptr`]) renders `*mut`/`*const <pointee-ABI>`; a NON-`char` pointee's
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)/// wrapper speaks the SAME raw-pointer type with NO cast (`Marshal::RawPtr` — a
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)/// `p as *mut c_int` self-cast would trip `clippy::unnecessary_cast`), but a
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)/// `char*` pointee is the canonical C string and the wrapper instead speaks an
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)/// owned `String`/borrowed `&str`, marshalling via a `CString`/`CStr` round-trip
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)/// (`Marshal::CStr`, PMAT-925 — the last decy ABI ceiling). The pointee MUST itself
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)/// be an ABI-mappable scalar — a pointer to a container/struct/another pointer
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)/// returns `None` (refuse-rather-than-mis-marshal, the same posture as the scalar
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)/// arms). Returns `None` for any non-ABI-mappable type.
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)struct CAbi {
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)    /// The `extern "C"` ABI type (e.g. `::std::os::raw::c_int`, `*mut c_char`).
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)    abi: String,
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    /// The native type the safe wrapper's signature speaks as a PARAMETER
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)    /// (e.g. `i64`, `*mut c_char`, or — for a C string — `&str`).
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    native_param: String,
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    /// The native type the safe wrapper's signature speaks as a RETURN
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    /// (e.g. `i64`, `*mut c_char`, or — for a C string — `String`). Differs from
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)    /// `native_param` only for a borrowing marshal like `Marshal::CStr` (`&str`
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    /// in, owned `String` out).
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)    native_ret: String,
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)    /// How the wrapper bridges `native` ↔ `abi`.
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)    marshal: Marshal,
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)}
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)fn c_abi_render(ty: &Type) -> Option<CAbi> {
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)    match ty {
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)        Type::Ptr { mutable, pointee } => {
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)            // The pointee must be a directly-ABI-mappable scalar; a pointer to a
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)            // non-mappable type (container/struct/another pointer) is refused —
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)            // decy never produces such a pointee, but the emitter is the last
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)            // ABI-honesty gate.
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)            let inner = c_abi_type(pointee)?;
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)            let qualifier = if *mutable { "mut" } else { "const" };
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)            let ptr = format!("*{qualifier} {inner}");
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)            // PMAT-925: a `char*` is the canonical C string — marshal it to/from
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)            // a Rust `String`/`&str` instead of leaking a raw `*mut c_char` to the
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)            // caller. Every other pointee stays a pass-through raw pointer.
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)            if matches!(pointee.as_ref(), Type::CChar) {
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)                Some(CAbi {
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)                    abi: ptr,
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)                    native_param: "&str".to_string(),
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)                    native_ret: "String".to_string(),
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)                    marshal: Marshal::CStr,
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)                })
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)            } else {
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)                Some(CAbi {
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)                    abi: ptr.clone(),
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)                    // The wrapper speaks the same raw-pointer type — no cast.
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)                    native_param: ptr.clone(),
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)                    native_ret: ptr,
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)                    marshal: Marshal::RawPtr,
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)                })
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)            }
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)        }
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)        scalar => {
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)            let abi = c_abi_type(scalar)?.to_string();
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)            let native = wrapper_native(scalar).to_string();
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)            Some(CAbi {
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)                native_param: native.clone(),
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)                native_ret: native,
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)                marshal: Marshal::ScalarCast,
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)                abi,
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)            })
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)        }
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)    }
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)}
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)/// PMAT-898 (Sprint-2 Tier 2): resolve each module's FFI-boundary `to_lang` from
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)/// the full dispatched module set. A single-file frontend can't see its siblings,
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)/// so `depyler-frontend::detect_ffi_boundaries` records a PROVISIONAL `to_lang`
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)/// (C, the canonical CPython-extension shape) for every relative import. With the
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)/// whole `Vec<Module>` in hand (the `xpile hybrid` CLI), rewrite each boundary's
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)/// `to_lang` to the `source_lang` of whichever sibling module actually DEFINES
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)/// the symbol. Consequences once `reconcile` runs:
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)///   - a relative import of a *Python* sibling becomes `Python → Python`, which
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)///     reconcile drops via its same-language skip (NOT a false FFI boundary);
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)///   - a relative import of a *C* sibling stays `Python → C` and resolves;
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)///   - a symbol no module defines is left as-is, so reconcile reports it
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)///     unresolved (the `manifest_completeness` invariant of C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT).
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)///
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)/// Call this BEFORE [`FfiManifest::reconcile`].
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)pub fn resolve_boundary_to_langs(modules: &mut [Module]) {
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)    // symbol -> source_lang of the first module that exports it.
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)    let mut exporters: HashMap<String, SourceLang> = HashMap::new();
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)    for m in modules.iter() {
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)        // PMAT-932: a Shell module exports its PROGRAM name (the file stem =
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)        // `Module::name`), the thing a subprocess shim spawns — not a meta-HIR
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)        // item (its only item is the synthetic `main` placeholder). Register it
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)        // so a Python `from ._tool import _tool` boundary resolves Python→Shell.
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)        if m.source_lang == SourceLang::Shell {
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)            exporters.entry(m.name.clone()).or_insert(SourceLang::Shell);
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)        }
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)        for it in &m.items {
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)            if let Some(name) = item_exported_name(it) {
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)                exporters.entry(name.to_string()).or_insert(m.source_lang);
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)            }
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)        }
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)    }
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)    for m in modules.iter_mut() {
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)        for b in &mut m.ffi_boundaries {
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)            if let Some(&lang) = exporters.get(&b.symbol) {
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)                b.to_lang = lang;
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)            }
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)        }
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)    }
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)}
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)

[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)mod tests {
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)    use super::*;
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)    use xpile_meta_hir::{Block, Expr, Function, Type};
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)    fn module(name: &str, lang: SourceLang, boundaries: Vec<FfiBoundary>) -> Module {
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)        Module {
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)            name: name.to_string(),
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)            source_lang: lang,
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)            items: Vec::new(),
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)            ffi_boundaries: boundaries,
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)        }
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)    }
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)    /// A module of `lang` that DEFINES (exports) `symbol` as the FFI-callable
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)    /// target reconciliation requires.
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)    ///
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)    /// PMAT-932: the export SURFACE differs by paradigm. A code module exports a
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)    /// named item (function) — so the item is named `symbol`. A **Shell** module
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)    /// is invoked as a subprocess by its PROGRAM name (the file stem =
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)    /// `Module::name`), and its only meta-HIR item is the synthetic `main`
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)    /// placeholder (exactly what `bashrs-frontend` produces) — so for Shell the
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)    /// MODULE is named `symbol` and the item stays `main`. `name` is the module
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)    /// name for non-shell langs; it is overridden to `symbol` for Shell so the
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)    /// helper mirrors real bashrs output.
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)    fn module_defining(name: &str, lang: SourceLang, symbol: &str) -> Module {
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)        let is_shell = lang == SourceLang::Shell;
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)        let item_name = if is_shell { "main" } else { symbol };
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)        let module_name = if is_shell { symbol } else { name };
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)        Module {
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)            name: module_name.to_string(),
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)            source_lang: lang,
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)            items: vec![Item::Function(Function {
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)                name: item_name.to_string(),
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)                params: Vec::new(),
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)                return_type: Type::I64,
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)                body: Block {
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)                    stmts: Vec::new(),
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)                    trailing_return: Expr::LitInt(0),
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)                },
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)            })],
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)            ffi_boundaries: Vec::new(),
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)        }
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)    }
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)    fn boundary(from: SourceLang, to: SourceLang, symbol: &str) -> FfiBoundary {
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)        FfiBoundary {
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)            from_lang: from,
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)            to_lang: to,
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)            symbol: symbol.to_string(),
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)            signature: format!("{symbol}(...)"),
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)        }
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)    }
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)    /// A C module defining `symbol` as a function with the given params/return —
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)    /// the typed export side the shim emitter recovers signatures from.
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)    fn c_fn(name: &str, params: Vec<(&str, Type)>, ret: Type) -> Module {
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)        Module {
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)            name: name.to_string(),
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)            source_lang: SourceLang::C,
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)            items: vec![Item::Function(Function {
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)                name: name.to_string(),
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)                params: params
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)                    .into_iter()
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)                    .map(|(n, ty)| xpile_meta_hir::Param {
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)                        name: n.to_string(),
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)                        ty,
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)                        mutable: false,
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)                    })
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)                    .collect(),
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)                return_type: ret,
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)                body: Block {
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)                    stmts: Vec::new(),
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)                    trailing_return: Expr::LitInt(0),
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)                },
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)            })],
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)            ffi_boundaries: Vec::new(),
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)        }
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)    }
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)    /// Build [py-with-boundary, c-defining-fn], resolve + reconcile, and emit.
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)    fn emit_for(
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)        symbol: &str,
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)        params: Vec<(&str, Type)>,
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)        ret: Type,
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)    ) -> Result<String, FfiEmitError> {
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)        let mut modules = vec![
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)            module(
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)                "app",
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)                SourceLang::Python,
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)                vec![boundary(SourceLang::Python, SourceLang::C, symbol)],
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)            ),
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)            c_fn(symbol, params, ret),
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)        ];
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)        resolve_boundary_to_langs(&mut modules);
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)        let manifest = FfiManifest::reconcile(&modules).expect("reconciles");
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)        manifest.emit_rust_shims(&modules)
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)    }

[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)    fn c_abi_type_table() {
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)        assert_eq!(c_abi_type(&Type::I64), Some("::std::os::raw::c_int"));
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)        assert_eq!(c_abi_type(&Type::Bool), Some("::std::os::raw::c_int"));
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)        assert_eq!(c_abi_type(&Type::F64), Some("::std::os::raw::c_double"));
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)        // PMAT-911: a 32-bit C float rides the DISTINCT c_float slot — never
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)        // widened through the 64-bit c_double.
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)        assert_eq!(
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)            c_abi_type(&Type::F32),
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_float"),
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)            "float must ride the 32-bit c_float ABI slot, not c_double"
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)        );
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)        assert_ne!(
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)            c_abi_type(&Type::F32),
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)            c_abi_type(&Type::F64),
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)            "F32 and F64 must map to distinct C ABI slots"
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)        );
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)        assert_eq!(wrapper_native(&Type::F32), "f32");
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)        // PMAT-909: a wider C integer is NOT narrowed to c_int.
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)        assert_eq!(
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)            c_abi_type(&Type::CLong),
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_longlong"),
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)            "long/int64_t must ride the 64-bit c_longlong ABI slot, not c_int"
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)        );
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)        assert_eq!(wrapper_native(&Type::CLong), "i64");
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)        // PMAT-918: a 32-bit UNSIGNED C int rides the DISTINCT c_uint slot —
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)        // never the signed c_int (a value ≥ 2³¹ would otherwise flip sign).
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)        assert_eq!(
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)            c_abi_type(&Type::CUInt),
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_uint"),
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)            "unsigned/uint32_t must ride the unsigned c_uint ABI slot, not c_int"
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)        );
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)        assert_ne!(
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)            c_abi_type(&Type::CUInt),
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)            c_abi_type(&Type::I64),
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)            "CUInt and I64 must map to distinct (signedness) C ABI slots"
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)        );
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)        assert_eq!(
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)            wrapper_native(&Type::CUInt),
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)            "u32",
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)            "unsigned wrapper must speak u32, never fall through to the i64 default"
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)        );
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)        // PMAT-921: a 64-bit UNSIGNED C int rides the DISTINCT c_ulonglong slot —
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)        // never the 32-bit c_uint (truncation) nor the signed c_longlong (a
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)        // value ≥ 2⁶³ would otherwise flip sign).
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)        assert_eq!(
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)            c_abi_type(&Type::CULong),
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_ulonglong"),
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)            "unsigned long/uint64_t must ride the unsigned 64-bit c_ulonglong ABI slot"
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)        );
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)        assert_ne!(
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)            c_abi_type(&Type::CULong),
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)            c_abi_type(&Type::CLong),
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)            "CULong and CLong must map to distinct (signedness) C ABI slots"
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)        );
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)        assert_ne!(
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)            c_abi_type(&Type::CULong),
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)            c_abi_type(&Type::CUInt),
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)            "CULong and CUInt must map to distinct (width) C ABI slots"
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)        );
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)        assert_eq!(
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)            wrapper_native(&Type::CULong),
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)            "u64",

[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)        );
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)        for ty in [

[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)            Type::Set(Box::new(Type::I64)),
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)            Type::Tuple(vec![Type::I64]),
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)            Type::BigInt,
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)            Type::Optional(Box::new(Type::I64)),

[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)        ] {

[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)    #[test]
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    fn c_abi_render_pointer_is_abi_honest_no_cast() {
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)        // PMAT-924: a non-`char` C pointer (`int*`) renders as a raw `*mut c_int`
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)        // whose native form IS the ABI form (RawPtr, no cast — a self-cast would
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)        // trip clippy::unnecessary_cast). A bare `int` still casts (i64 -> c_int).
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)        let p = c_abi_render(&Type::Ptr {
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)            mutable: true,
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)            pointee: Box::new(Type::I64),
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)        })
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)        .expect("int* is ABI-mappable");
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)        assert_eq!(p.abi, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_int");
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)        assert_eq!(p.native_param, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_int");
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)        assert_eq!(p.native_ret, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_int");
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)        assert!(
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)            matches!(p.marshal, Marshal::RawPtr),
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)            "a non-char raw pointer is its own native form — no marshalling"
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)        );
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)        // PMAT-925: `char*` is the canonical C string — the ABI slot is still a
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)        // raw `*mut c_char`, but the wrapper speaks `&str` in / owned `String`
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)        // out and marshals via a CString/CStr round-trip (Marshal::CStr).
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)        let pc = c_abi_render(&Type::Ptr {
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)            mutable: true,
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)            pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)        })
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)        .expect("char* is ABI-mappable");
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)        assert_eq!(pc.abi, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_char");
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)        assert_eq!(pc.native_param, "&str", "char* param speaks &str");
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)        assert_eq!(pc.native_ret, "String", "char* return speaks owned String");
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)        assert!(
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)            matches!(pc.marshal, Marshal::CStr),
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)            "char* marshals via CString/CStr, not a raw pointer pass-through"
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)        );
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)        // A scalar still needs the i64 -> c_int cast.
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)        let s = c_abi_render(&Type::I64).expect("scalar");
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)        assert!(
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)            matches!(s.marshal, Marshal::ScalarCast),
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)            "a scalar param casts to its C ABI slot"
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)        );
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)        // Refuse-rather-than-mis-marshal: a pointer to a NON-mappable pointee
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)        // (a container) is refused (None), not silently emitted.
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)        assert!(
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)            c_abi_render(&Type::Ptr {
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)                mutable: true,
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)                pointee: Box::new(Type::Str),
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)            })
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)            .is_none(),
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)            "pointer to a non-ABI-mappable pointee must be refused"
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)        );
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)    }

[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)    #[test]
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)    fn emit_shims_pointer_param_compiles_abi_honest() {
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)        // PMAT-924/925 end-to-end: a C `char*` param marshals to `&str` (PMAT-925)
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)        // while a NON-char `int*` param stays an ABI-honest raw pointer (PMAT-924).
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)        // The extern decl keeps both as raw pointers; the wrapper speaks `&str`
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)        // for the string and the raw pointer for `int*`, compiling under
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)        // -D warnings (the load-bearing gate — no unnecessary self-cast).
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)        let out = emit_for(
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)            "scan",
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)            vec![
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)                (
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)                    "s",
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)                    Type::Ptr {
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)                        mutable: true,
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)                        pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)                    },
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)                ),
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)                (
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)                    "out",
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)                    Type::Ptr {
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)                        mutable: true,
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)                        pointee: Box::new(Type::I64),
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)                    },
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)                ),
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)            ],
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)            Type::I64,
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)        )
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)        .expect("emits");
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)        assert!(
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)            out.contains(
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)                "fn scan(s: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char, out: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_int) -> ::std::os::raw::c_int;"
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)            ),
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)            "ABI-honest raw-pointer extern decl (both params stay raw pointers): {out}"
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)        );
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)        // PMAT-925: the `char*` param surfaces as `&str`, the `int*` stays raw.
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)        assert!(
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)            out.contains("pub fn scan_shim(s: &str, out: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_int) -> i64 {"),
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)            "wrapper marshals char* -> &str, keeps int* raw: {out}"
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)        );
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)        // The CString is bound BEFORE the unsafe call (so its buffer outlives it).
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)        assert!(
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)            out.contains("let __c_s = ::std::ffi::CString::new(s).expect(")
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)                && out.contains("__c_s.as_ptr() as *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char"),
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)            "char* param marshals via a pre-call CString binding: {out}"
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)        );
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)        // The non-char `int*` arg must NOT be self-cast (clippy::unnecessary_cast).

[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)            !out.contains("out as *mut"),
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)            "a raw int* arg must not be self-cast: {out}"
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)        );

[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)    fn emit_shims_cstr_roundtrip_marshals_string() {
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)        // PMAT-925 — the LAST decy ABI ceiling: a `char* upper(char*)` boundary
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)        // marshals a borrowed `&str` IN (via a NUL-checked CString whose buffer
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)        // outlives the call) and an owned `String` OUT (via a CStr view). The
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)        // safe wrapper NEVER exposes a raw `*mut c_char` — `unsafe` raw-pointer
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)        // handling is confined to the shim. The extern decl stays ABI-honest raw
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)        // pointers; the whole thing compiles under -D warnings.
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)        let out = emit_for(
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)            "upper",
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)            vec![(
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)                "s",
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)                Type::Ptr {
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)                    mutable: true,
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)                    pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)                },
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)            )],
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)            Type::Ptr {
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)                mutable: true,
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)                pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)            },
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)        )
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)        .expect("emits");
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)        // ABI boundary: both sides are raw `*mut c_char` in the extern block.
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)        assert!(
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)            out.contains(
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)                "fn upper(s: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char) -> *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char;"
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)            ),
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)            "extern decl keeps raw c_char pointers: {out}"
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)        );
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)        // Safe surface: `&str` in, owned `String` out — no raw pointer leaks.
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)        assert!(
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)            out.contains("pub fn upper_shim(s: &str) -> String {"),
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)            "wrapper marshals char* both ways to &str/String: {out}"
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)        );
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)        assert!(
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)            !out.contains("_shim(s: *mut"),
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)            "the safe wrapper must NOT expose a raw *mut c_char: {out}"
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)        );
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)        // Param marshal: a pre-call NUL-checked CString, borrowed for the call.
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)        assert!(
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)            out.contains("let __c_s = ::std::ffi::CString::new(s).expect(")
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)                && out.contains("__c_s.as_ptr() as *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char"),
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)            "char* param marshals via a pre-call CString binding: {out}"
[1898](https://docs.rs#1898)        );
[1899](https://docs.rs#1899)        // Return marshal: a CStr view copied into an owned String (lossy-UTF-8 to
[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)        // stay total on non-UTF-8 bytes).
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)        assert!(
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)            out.contains(
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)                "unsafe { ::std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr(__r).to_string_lossy().into_owned() }"
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)            ),
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)            "char* return marshals via a CStr -> owned String view: {out}"
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)        );
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)        assert!(
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)            rustc_lib_compiles("cstr", &out),
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)            "emitted CStr-marshalling shim must compile under -D warnings"
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)        );
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)    }

[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)    /// Compile `src` as a standalone Rust lib under `-D warnings`, on BOTH
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)    /// edition 2021 and edition 2024. Returns `true` if rustc is unavailable
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)    /// (constrained CI skips the gate) or the source compiles under every
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)    /// edition. The emitted shim is meant to be dropped into a user crate of
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)    /// unknown edition — and `cargo new` defaults to 2024 — so a 2021-only gate
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)    /// would mask the bare-`extern "C"` regression (a hard error in 2024). `tag`
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)    /// keeps concurrent compile-gate tests off each other's temp files (a bare
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)    /// pid collides when tests run in parallel threads).
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)    fn rustc_lib_compiles(tag: &str, src: &str) -> bool {
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)        if std::process::Command::new("rustc")
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)            .arg("--version")
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)            .output()
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)            .is_err()
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)        {
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)            eprintln!("rustc unavailable — skipping compile gate");
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)            return true;
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)        }
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)        let dir = std::env::temp_dir();
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)        let pid = std::process::id();
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)        for edition in ["2021", "2024"] {
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)            let src_path = dir.join(format!("xpile_shim_gate_{tag}_{edition}_{pid}.rs"));
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)            let rlib = dir.join(format!("libxpile_shim_gate_{tag}_{edition}_{pid}.rlib"));
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)            std::fs::write(&src_path, src).expect("write shim");
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)            let status = std::process::Command::new("rustc")
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)                .args([
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)                    "--crate-type",
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)                    "lib",
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)                    "--edition",
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)                    edition,
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)                    "-D",
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)                    "warnings",
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)                ])
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)                .arg(&src_path)
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)                .arg("-o")
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)                .arg(&rlib)
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)                .status()
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)                .expect("spawn rustc");
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&src_path);
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&rlib);
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)            if !status.success() {
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)                eprintln!("emitted shim failed to compile under edition {edition}");
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)                return false;
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)            }
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)        }
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)        true
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)    }
[1988](https://docs.rs#1988)
[1989](https://docs.rs#1989)    #[test]
[1990](https://docs.rs#1990)    fn emit_shims_output_compiles_under_rustc() {
[1991](https://docs.rs#1991)        // The load-bearing gate: the emitted shim is type/arity/ABI compile-
[1992](https://docs.rs#1992)        // checkable with NO C object (the extern symbol stays unresolved at lib
[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)        // build). Gated on rustc being spawnable so constrained CI skips it.
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)        let out = emit_for("square_sum", vec![("x", Type::I64)], Type::I64).expect("emits");
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)        assert!(
[1996](https://docs.rs#1996)            rustc_lib_compiles("c", &out),
[1997](https://docs.rs#1997)            "emitted C shim must compile under -D warnings"
[1998](https://docs.rs#1998)        );
[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)    }
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)
[2001](https://docs.rs#2001)    /// Build [driver-module-with-boundary, target-module-defining-symbol],
[2002](https://docs.rs#2002)    /// resolve `to_lang` from the exporting sibling, reconcile, and emit — the
[2003](https://docs.rs#2003)    /// generic shape behind the per-paradigm tests below.
[2004](https://docs.rs#2004)    fn emit_cross(
[2005](https://docs.rs#2005)        from: SourceLang,
[2006](https://docs.rs#2006)        target: SourceLang,
[2007](https://docs.rs#2007)        symbol: &str,
[2008](https://docs.rs#2008)    ) -> Result<String, FfiEmitError> {
[2009](https://docs.rs#2009)        let mut modules = vec![
[2010](https://docs.rs#2010)            module("driver", from, vec![boundary(from, target, symbol)]),
[2011](https://docs.rs#2011)            module_defining("target", target, symbol),
[2012](https://docs.rs#2012)        ];
[2013](https://docs.rs#2013)        resolve_boundary_to_langs(&mut modules);
[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)        assert_eq!(
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)            modules[0].ffi_boundaries[0].to_lang, target,
[2016](https://docs.rs#2016)            "to_lang should resolve to the exporting sibling"
[2017](https://docs.rs#2017)        );
[2018](https://docs.rs#2018)        let manifest = FfiManifest::reconcile(&modules).expect("reconciles");
[2019](https://docs.rs#2019)        manifest.emit_rust_shims(&modules)
[2020](https://docs.rs#2020)    }

[2048](https://docs.rs#2048)    #[test]
[2049](https://docs.rs#2049)    fn emit_shims_cpp_boundary_emits_pybind11_shim() {
[2050](https://docs.rs#2050)        // PMAT-927: a Rust→C++ boundary now lowers to a real pybind11 shim (was
[2051](https://docs.rs#2051)        // an `Err(pybind11 gap)`). The C++ symbol is name-mangled, so the shim
[2052](https://docs.rs#2052)        // calls the pybind11-registered binding by its Python-visible name
[2053](https://docs.rs#2053)        // through the embedded interpreter — never a guessed `extern "C"`.
[2054](https://docs.rs#2054)        // `module_defining` exports `kernel` as a nullary `-> i64` in module
[2055](https://docs.rs#2055)        // "target"; from != to (Rust→Cpp) so reconcile keeps the boundary.
[2056](https://docs.rs#2056)        let out = emit_cross(SourceLang::Rust, SourceLang::Cpp, "kernel").expect("emits");
[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)        // No extern block / no unsafe in the EMITTED CODE: a mangled C++ symbol
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)        // must NOT be declared as a flat C symbol (it would mis-link), and the
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)        // honest path goes through pybind11. The doc-comment prose names both
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)        // `extern "C"` and `unsafe` to explain WHY they are absent, so scan only
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)        // non-comment lines for the actual tokens.
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)        let code_only: String = out
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)            .lines()
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)            .filter(|l| !l.trim_start().starts_with("//") && !l.trim_start().starts_with("///"))
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)            .join("\n");
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)        assert!(
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)            !code_only.contains("extern \"C\""),
[2069](https://docs.rs#2069)            "a name-mangled C++ symbol must not be declared extern \"C\": {out}"
[2070](https://docs.rs#2070)        );
[2071](https://docs.rs#2071)        assert!(
[2072](https://docs.rs#2072)            !code_only.contains("unsafe"),
[2073](https://docs.rs#2073)            "the pybind11 wrapper code is unsafe-free: {out}"
[2074](https://docs.rs#2074)        );
[2075](https://docs.rs#2075)        assert!(
[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)            out.contains("pub fn kernel_shim() -> i64 {"),
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)            "nullary -> i64 pybind11 wrapper: {out}"
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)        );
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)        // Embeds the interpreter, imports the pybind11 EXTENSION module by name,
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)        // and getattrs the Python-visible binding name (not a mangled symbol).
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)        assert!(out.contains("::pyo3::Python::with_gil(|py|"), "{out}");
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)        assert!(
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)            out.contains("::pyo3::types::PyModule::import(py, \"target\")"),
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)            "imports the pybind11 module by name: {out}"
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)        );
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)        assert!(out.contains(".getattr(\"kernel\")"), "{out}");
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)        assert!(out.contains(".call1(())"), "0-arg call passes (): {out}");
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)        assert!(
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)            out.contains(".extract().expect("),
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)            "non-Unit return is extracted: {out}"
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)        );
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)        // Honesty: the wrapper doc names the mangling reality + the pybind11 binding.
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)        assert!(
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)            out.contains("name-mangled") && out.contains("m.def"),

[2264](https://docs.rs#2264)            .lines()

[2282](https://docs.rs#2282)        );
[2283](https://docs.rs#2283)        assert!(out.contains(".getattr(\"embed\")"), "{out}");
[2284](https://docs.rs#2284)        // A 0-arg call passes the empty tuple; the result is extracted to i64.

[2286](https://docs.rs#2286)        assert!(

[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)    #[test]
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)    fn emit_pyo3_shim_compiles_against_pyo3() {
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)        // The load-bearing gate (mirrors the C arm's rustc compile gate, but for
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)        // a real external dep): the emitted pyo3 shim must COMPILE against pyo3.
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)        // pyo3 needs libpython at LINK time, but `cargo check` only TYPE-checks,
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)        // so a Python *dev* install (headers via pyo3-build) suffices and no
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)        // interpreter must run. Gated on cargo + a buildable pyo3 — skips
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)        // gracefully (returns) when pyo3 cannot be built (offline / no python).
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)        let out = emit_cross(SourceLang::Rust, SourceLang::Python, "embed").expect("emits");
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)        pyo3_shim_checks(&out);
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)    }
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)    /// `cargo check` the emitted pyo3 shim as a tiny standalone crate that
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)    /// depends on pyo3 (`auto-initialize` so no `Python::initialize` boilerplate
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)    /// is needed for a type-check). Skips (returns) gracefully if `cargo` is
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)    /// absent or pyo3 cannot be resolved/built (offline CI / no Python dev
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)    /// headers) — the structural string assertions above always run; this adds
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)    /// the real-compiler gate when the toolchain is present.
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)    fn pyo3_shim_checks(shim: &str) {
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)        if std::process::Command::new("cargo")
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)            .arg("--version")
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)            .output()
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)            .is_err()
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)        {
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)            eprintln!("cargo unavailable — skipping pyo3 compile gate");
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)            return;
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)        }
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)            "xpile_pyo3_gate_{}_{:?}",
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)            std::process::id(),
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469)            std::thread::current().id()
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)        ));
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)        if std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src")).is_err() {
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)            eprintln!("temp dir unavailable — skipping pyo3 compile gate");
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)            return;
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)        }
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)        // pyo3 0.23 — pinned minor so the emitted `PyModule::import`/`call1`/
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)        // `extract` API surface is stable. `auto-initialize` lets a type-check
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)        // proceed without an explicit interpreter init.
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)        std::fs::write(
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)            dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)            "[package]\nname = \"xpile-pyo3-gate\"\nversion = \"0.0.0\"\nedition = \"2021\"\n\n[dependencies]\npyo3 = { version = \"0.23\", features = [\"auto-initialize\"] }\n",
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)        )
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)        .expect("write Cargo.toml");
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)        std::fs::write(dir.join("src").join("lib.rs"), shim).expect("write shim");
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)        let out = std::process::Command::new("cargo")
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)            .current_dir(&dir)
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)            .arg("check")
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)            .arg("--target-dir")
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)            .arg(dir.join("target"))
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)            .output();
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)        match out {
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)            Ok(o) if o.status.success() => {}
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)            Ok(o) => {
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)                let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stderr);
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)                // A pyo3/libpython *resolution or build* failure (no Python dev
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)                // env, offline) is a SKIP, not a test failure — the structural
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)                // assertions already validated the shim shape. Only a genuine
[2498](https://docs.rs#2498)                // type error in OUR emitted code should fail. Heuristic: if the
[2499](https://docs.rs#2499)                // failure mentions one of our shim symbols (`_shim`) it's our bug;
[2500](https://docs.rs#2500)                // otherwise it's an environment/dep issue → skip.
[2501](https://docs.rs#2501)                if stderr.contains("error[") && stderr.contains("_shim") {
[2502](https://docs.rs#2502)                    panic!("emitted pyo3 shim failed to type-check:\n{stderr}");
[2503](https://docs.rs#2503)                }
[2504](https://docs.rs#2504)                eprintln!(
[2505](https://docs.rs#2505)                    "pyo3 could not be built (offline / no Python dev env) — skipping pyo3 compile gate"
[2506](https://docs.rs#2506)                );
[2507](https://docs.rs#2507)            }
[2508](https://docs.rs#2508)            Err(_) => eprintln!("cargo spawn failed — skipping pyo3 compile gate"),
[2509](https://docs.rs#2509)        }
[2510](https://docs.rs#2510)        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
[2511](https://docs.rs#2511)    }

[2533](https://docs.rs#2533)            !out.contains("unsafe"),

[2537](https://docs.rs#2537)            !out.contains("xpile-contract:"),

[2540](https://docs.rs#2540)        // Compiles when the same-crate callee is in scope (the real workspace
[2541](https://docs.rs#2541)        // context: main.rs defines `helper`, the shim forwards to it). Appended
[2542](https://docs.rs#2542)        // AFTER the shim so the file's `#![allow(dead_code)]` inner attribute

[2546](https://docs.rs#2546)            rustc_lib_compiles("ruchy", &with_callee),

[2548](https://docs.rs#2548)        );
[2549](https://docs.rs#2549)    }
