[2721](https://docs.rs#2721)    fn emit_shims_cuint_boundary_maps_c_uint() {
[2722](https://docs.rs#2722)        // PMAT-918: an `unsigned`/`uint32_t` C boundary rides the UNSIGNED
[2723](https://docs.rs#2723)        // c_uint ABI slot (NOT the signed c_int) with a u32 wrapper — the decy
[2724](https://docs.rs#2724)        // unsigned-int lift. Compiles end-to-end under -D warnings.
[2725](https://docs.rs#2725)        let out = emit_for("uwrap", vec![("x", Type::CUInt)], Type::CUInt).expect("emits");
[2726](https://docs.rs#2726)        assert!(
[2727](https://docs.rs#2727)            out.contains("fn uwrap(x: ::std::os::raw::c_uint) -> ::std::os::raw::c_uint;"),
[2728](https://docs.rs#2728)            "unsigned boundary must use c_uint, not c_int:\n{out}"
[2729](https://docs.rs#2729)        );
[2730](https://docs.rs#2730)        assert!(out.contains("pub fn uwrap_shim(x: u32) -> u32 {"));
[2731](https://docs.rs#2731)        assert!(out.contains("x as ::std::os::raw::c_uint"));
[2732](https://docs.rs#2732)        assert!(out.contains("__r as u32"));
[2733](https://docs.rs#2733)        // An unsigned boundary must NEVER ride the signed c_int (signedness flip).
[2734](https://docs.rs#2734)        let extern_block = out
[2735](https://docs.rs#2735)            .split("extern \"C\" {")
[2736](https://docs.rs#2736)            .nth(1)
[2737](https://docs.rs#2737)            .unwrap()
[2738](https://docs.rs#2738)            .split('}')
[2739](https://docs.rs#2739)            .next()
[2740](https://docs.rs#2740)            .unwrap();
[2741](https://docs.rs#2741)        assert!(
[2742](https://docs.rs#2742)            !extern_block.contains("c_int"),
[2743](https://docs.rs#2743)            "a CUInt boundary must not ride the signed c_int:\n{extern_block}"
[2744](https://docs.rs#2744)        );
[2745](https://docs.rs#2745)        assert!(
[2746](https://docs.rs#2746)            rustc_lib_compiles("cuint", &out),
[2747](https://docs.rs#2747)            "emitted c_uint shim must compile under -D warnings"
[2748](https://docs.rs#2748)        );
[2749](https://docs.rs#2749)    }
[2750](https://docs.rs#2750)
[2751](https://docs.rs#2751)    #[test]
[2752](https://docs.rs#2752)    fn emit_shims_culong_boundary_maps_c_ulonglong() {
[2753](https://docs.rs#2753)        // PMAT-921: an `unsigned long`/`uint64_t` C boundary rides the UNSIGNED
[2754](https://docs.rs#2754)        // 64-bit c_ulonglong ABI slot (NOT the 32-bit c_uint, NOT the signed
[2755](https://docs.rs#2755)        // c_longlong) with a u64 wrapper — the decy unsigned-long lift. Compiles
[2756](https://docs.rs#2756)        // end-to-end under -D warnings.
[2757](https://docs.rs#2757)        let out = emit_for("ulwrap", vec![("x", Type::CULong)], Type::CULong).expect("emits");
[2758](https://docs.rs#2758)        assert!(
[2759](https://docs.rs#2759)            out.contains(
[2760](https://docs.rs#2760)                "fn ulwrap(x: ::std::os::raw::c_ulonglong) -> ::std::os::raw::c_ulonglong;"
[2761](https://docs.rs#2761)            ),
[2762](https://docs.rs#2762)            "unsigned long boundary must use c_ulonglong:\n{out}"
[2763](https://docs.rs#2763)        );
[2764](https://docs.rs#2764)        assert!(out.contains("pub fn ulwrap_shim(x: u64) -> u64 {"));
[2765](https://docs.rs#2765)        assert!(out.contains("x as ::std::os::raw::c_ulonglong"));
[2766](https://docs.rs#2766)        assert!(out.contains("__r as u64"));
[2767](https://docs.rs#2767)        // A 64-bit unsigned boundary must ride neither the 32-bit c_uint
[2768](https://docs.rs#2768)        // (truncation) nor the signed c_longlong (signedness flip).
[2769](https://docs.rs#2769)        let extern_block = out
[2770](https://docs.rs#2770)            .split("extern \"C\" {")

[2777](https://docs.rs#2777)            !extern_block.contains("c_uint")
[2778](https://docs.rs#2778)                && !extern_block.contains("c_int")
[2779](https://docs.rs#2779)                && !extern_block.contains("c_longlong"),
[2780](https://docs.rs#2780)            "a CULong boundary must ride only the unsigned 64-bit c_ulonglong:\n{extern_block}"
[2781](https://docs.rs#2781)        );
[2782](https://docs.rs#2782)        assert!(
[2783](https://docs.rs#2783)            rustc_lib_compiles("culong", &out),

# FfiEmitError in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/struct.FfiEmitError.html

## Expand description

PMAT-899 (Sprint-2 Tier 2): a reconciled boundary could not be lowered to a
Rust FFI shim because a recovered parameter/return type has no ABI-honest C
mapping (a pointer/string/struct/container the first-cut emitter refuses
rather than mis-marshal). Mirrors [ FfiReconcileError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiReconcileError.html): surfacing the gap
beats emitting a wrong-ABI shim.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#221-266)

#### pub fn [reconcile](https://docs.rs#method.reconcile)(modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FfiManifest](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html), [FfiReconcileError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiReconcileError.html)>

Phase 2 of the hybrid transpile flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
reconcile every cross-language FFI boundary across the dispatched modules
into a single manifest, or fail listing the unresolved boundaries.

A boundary `{from_lang, to_lang, symbol, signature}` is a call that
crosses from `from_lang` into `to_lang`. It RESOLVES when a sibling module
of `to_lang` is present in the dispatched set (the target language was
actually transpiled). Each resolved boundary becomes an [ FfiEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEntry.html) with a
deterministic

`shim_id`; any boundary whose target language is absent fails
reconciliation (the `manifest_completeness` invariant of
`C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT`). Same-language boundaries (`from == to`) are no-ops.PMAT-895: resolution is SYMBOL-LEVEL — a boundary resolves only when a
module of `to_lang` actually DEFINES an item (function/const) named
`symbol`. A target-language module that is present but does NOT export the
symbol still fails reconciliation (the `manifest_completeness` invariant is
about the symbol crossing the line, not just the language being present).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#304-391)#### pub fn [emit_rust_shims](https://docs.rs#method.emit_rust_shims)(
    &self,
    modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [FfiEmitError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEmitError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#304-391)

#### pub fn [emit_rust_shims](https://docs.rs#method.emit_rust_shims)(
    &self,
    modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [FfiEmitError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEmitError.html)>

PMAT-899 — Phase 4 of the hybrid flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
emit a self-contained Rust FFI shim file for every reconciled
cross-language boundary, dispatched per target paradigm. `modules` is the
same set passed to [ reconcile](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.reconcile) — it is the ONLY source
of real param/return types (an

[carries placeholder signatures).](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEntry.html)

`FfiEntry`Per-paradigm strategy (see [`shim_part_for`]):

- **C**→ a real- `extern "C"`foreign declaration + a safe- `*_shim`wrapper confining- `unsafe`, citing- `C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT`.
- **Shell**→ a real- `std::process::Command`-based wrapper (shell speaks argv + exit codes — no C ABI, no- `unsafe`), citing- `C-FFI-SHELL-SUBPROCESS`.
- **Ruchy / Rust**→ a real same-crate direct-call forwarder (both lower to native Rust in the same crate — a plain in-crate call, no- `unsafe`, no- `extern`).
- **Python**→ a real pyo3 CPython-embedding shim (PMAT-926): under the GIL it imports the defining module and calls the function, marshalling scalar args/return through pyo3 (- `i64`/- `f64`/- `bool`/- `String`).
- **Cpp**→ a real pybind11 C++ shim (PMAT-927): the C++ symbol is name-mangled, so this calls the pybind11-registered binding by its Python-visible name through the embedded interpreter (the same path Python uses), refusing rather than guessing a mangled- `extern "C"`. Six of seven arms are now real (C, Shell, Ruchy, Rust, Python, Cpp).
- **Cuda / Lean**→ a specific, mechanism-named- `FfiEmitError`

All-or-nothing (mirrors `reconcile`’s `manifest_completeness`): if ANY
boundary cannot be shimmed, nothing is emitted and the gaps are returned —
a half-shimmed hybrid build is not a build.

Compile-checkable WITHOUT the foreign object: a C extern symbol stays
unresolved at lib-build time and a shell shim needs no symbol at all, so
type/arity/ABI are validated by `rustc --crate-type lib` alone (linking is
only needed to *run*).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#407-447)#### pub fn [emit_hybrid_workspace](https://docs.rs#method.emit_hybrid_workspace)(
    &self,
    modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)],
    c_sources: &[([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))],
    rust_src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),

) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [WorkspaceEmitError](https://docs.rs/enum.WorkspaceEmitError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#407-447)

#### pub fn [emit_hybrid_workspace](https://docs.rs#method.emit_hybrid_workspace)(
    &self,
    modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)],
    c_sources: &[([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))],
    rust_src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    out_dir: &[Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [WorkspaceEmitError](https://docs.rs/enum.WorkspaceEmitError.html)>

PMAT-901 — Phase 5a of the hybrid flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
emit a self-contained, BUILDABLE Cargo workspace for the hybrid module.
Files: `Cargo.toml` (a bin crate); `build.rs` ([`HYBRID_BUILD_RS`] —
cc-compiles every `csrc/*.c` and links it); `csrc/<name>.c` (each C source
verbatim, from `c_sources`); `src/ffi_shims.rs` (the reconciled shims from
[ emit_rust_shims](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.emit_rust_shims)); and

`src/main.rs` (`rust_src`,
the caller’s lowering of the non-C modules, plus `mod ffi_shims;`).`cargo build` on the result compiles the Rust side AND cc-compiles + links
the C side through the emitted `extern "C"` shim — the first *executing*
hybrid artifact (Phase 5a). `rust_src` is supplied by the caller (the rust
backend’s lowering of the entry module) so this crate stays codegen-free.
All-or-nothing: an unshimmable boundary fails via [ FfiEmitError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEmitError.html) before
anything is written past the shim step.

# defining_function in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/fn.defining_function.html

## Expand description

Recover the real defining [ Function](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Function.html) for a reconciled entry, mirroring

[’s symbol/](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.reconcile)

`FfiManifest::reconcile``to_lang` match. `reconcile` guarantees an
entry exists only when the symbol is defined, so a miss here is an internal
invariant violation (surfaced as an unsupported boundary by the caller).
The defining function for a reconciled boundary: the `Item::Function` named
`entry.symbol` in the module whose `source_lang` is `entry.to_lang`. Public so
the `--verify` flow (PMAT-902) can read the C callee’s param/return types to
build the CPython-side ctypes ABI binding for the differential reference.

---

# resolve_boundary_to_langs in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/fn.resolve_boundary_to_langs.html

`pub fn resolve_boundary_to_langs(modules: &mut [`[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)])## Expand description

PMAT-898 (Sprint-2 Tier 2): resolve each module’s FFI-boundary `to_lang` from
the full dispatched module set. A single-file frontend can’t see its siblings,
so `depyler-frontend::detect_ffi_boundaries` records a PROVISIONAL `to_lang`
(C, the canonical CPython-extension shape) for every relative import. With the
whole `Vec<Module>` in hand (the `xpile hybrid` CLI), rewrite each boundary’s
`to_lang` to the `source_lang` of whichever sibling module actually DEFINES
the symbol. Consequences once `reconcile` runs:

- a relative import of a *Python*sibling becomes`Python → Python`, which reconcile drops via its same-language skip (NOT a false FFI boundary);
- a relative import of a *C*sibling stays`Python → C`and resolves;
- a symbol no module defines is left as-is, so reconcile reports it
unresolved (the `manifest_completeness`invariant of C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT).

Call this BEFORE [ FfiManifest::reconcile](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.reconcile).

---

# retype_float_ffi_sites in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/fn.retype_float_ffi_sites.html

`pub fn retype_float_ffi_sites(manifest: &`[FfiManifest](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html), modules: &mut [[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)])## Expand description

PMAT-931 (HUNT correctness — the PMAT-930 `c_double` two-arg divergence):
after reconciliation, re-type the FFI call sites of every reconciled symbol
whose `to_lang` definition returns `Type::F64` so the float-repr path is
selected in the calling (Python) module.

The Python frontend lowers `app.py` BEFORE the C sibling is dispatched, so a
call to a `double`-returning C symbol is typed with the unknown-callee I64
default. That makes `print(scale2(...))` print a whole double as `10` (not
Python’s `10.0`) and `let r: float = scale2(...)` emit `let r: i64` (rustc
E0308). This walks each non-`to_lang` module and corrects those sites via
[ xpile_meta_hir::retype_ffi_float_call_sites](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/fn.retype_ffi_float_call_sites.html). Idempotent / no-op when no
reconciled symbol returns F64.

# xpile_contract_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-contract-backend/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_contract_backend/

## Expand description

ContractBackend trait — proof-lane rendering abstraction.

Renders parsed [ xpile_contracts::Contract](https://docs.rs/xpile-contracts/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_contracts/struct.Contract.html) into LaTeX (math +
theorem environments), Lean 4 theorem text (with

`@[xpile_contract]`
attribute carrying the verbatim contract ID), or mdBook.Architectural invariants codified in
`contracts/xpile-contract-backend-trait-v1.yaml`. The citation bridge
uses **format-native structured constructs** parseable by the host
elaborator/parser, NOT regex over body text. See
`docs/specifications/sub/contract-backend-trait.md` §“Citation bridge”.

# serde_json - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_json/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-json)Serde JSON

JSON is a ubiquitous open-standard format that uses human-readable text to transmit data objects consisting of key-value pairs.

```
{
    "name": "John Doe",
    "age": 43,
    "address": {
        "street": "10 Downing Street",
        "city": "London"
    },
    "phones": [
        "+44 1234567",
        "+44 2345678"
    ]
}
```
There are three common ways that you might find yourself needing to work with JSON data in Rust.

- **As text data.**An unprocessed string of JSON data that you receive on an HTTP endpoint, read from a file, or prepare to send to a remote server.
- **As an untyped or loosely typed representation.**Maybe you want to check that some JSON data is valid before passing it on, but without knowing the structure of what it contains. Or you want to do very basic manipulations like insert a key in a particular spot.
- **As a strongly typed Rust data structure.**When you expect all or most of your data to conform to a particular structure and want to get real work done without JSON’s loosey-goosey nature tripping you up.

Serde JSON provides efficient, flexible, safe ways of converting data between each of these representations.

[§](https://docs.rs#operating-on-untyped-json-values)Operating on untyped JSON values

Any valid JSON data can be manipulated in the following recursive enum
representation. This data structure is [ serde_json::Value](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html).

```
enum Value {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(Number),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<Value>),
    Object(Map<String, Value>),
}
```
A string of JSON data can be parsed into a `serde_json::Value` by the
[ serde_json::from_str](https://docs.rs/fn.from_str.html) function. There is also

[for parsing from a byte slice](https://docs.rs/fn.from_slice.html)

`from_slice``&[u8]` and [for parsing from any](https://docs.rs/fn.from_reader.html)

`from_reader``io::Read` like a File or a TCP stream.```
use serde_json::{Result, Value};
fn untyped_example() -> Result<()> {
    // Some JSON input data as a &str. Maybe this comes from the user.
    let data = r#"
        {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "age": 43,
            "phones": [
                "+44 1234567",
                "+44 2345678"
            ]
        }"#;
    // Parse the string of data into serde_json::Value.
    let v: Value = serde_json::from_str(data)?;
    // Access parts of the data by indexing with square brackets.
    println!("Please call {} at the number {}", v["name"], v["phones"][0]);
    Ok(())
}
```
The result of square bracket indexing like `v["name"]` is a borrow of the
data at that index, so the type is `&Value`. A JSON map can be indexed with
string keys, while a JSON array can be indexed with integer keys. If the
type of the data is not right for the type with which it is being indexed,
or if a map does not contain the key being indexed, or if the index into a
vector is out of bounds, the returned element is `Value::Null`.

When a `Value` is printed, it is printed as a JSON string. So in the code
above, the output looks like `Please call "John Doe" at the number "+44 1234567"`. The quotation marks appear because `v["name"]` is a `&Value`
containing a JSON string and its JSON representation is `"John Doe"`.
Printing as a plain string without quotation marks involves converting from
a JSON string to a Rust string with [ as_str()](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html#method.as_str) or avoiding the use of

`Value` as described in the following section.The `Value` representation is sufficient for very basic tasks but can be
tedious to work with for anything more significant. Error handling is
verbose to implement correctly, for example imagine trying to detect the
presence of unrecognized fields in the input data. The compiler is powerless
to help you when you make a mistake, for example imagine typoing `v["name"]`
as `v["nmae"]` in one of the dozens of places it is used in your code.

[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-json-as-strongly-typed-data-structures)Parsing JSON as strongly typed data structures

Serde provides a powerful way of mapping JSON data into Rust data structures largely automatically.

```
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Result;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
fn typed_example() -> Result<()> {
    // Some JSON input data as a &str. Maybe this comes from the user.
    let data = r#"
        {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "age": 43,
            "phones": [
                "+44 1234567",
                "+44 2345678"
            ]
        }"#;
    // Parse the string of data into a Person object. This is exactly the
    // same function as the one that produced serde_json::Value above, but
    // now we are asking it for a Person as output.
    let p: Person = serde_json::from_str(data)?;
    // Do things just like with any other Rust data structure.
    println!("Please call {} at the number {}", p.name, p.phones[0]);
    Ok(())
}
```
This is the same `serde_json::from_str` function as before, but this time we
assign the return value to a variable of type `Person` so Serde will
automatically interpret the input data as a `Person` and produce informative
error messages if the layout does not conform to what a `Person` is expected
to look like.

Any type that implements Serde’s `Deserialize` trait can be deserialized
this way. This includes built-in Rust standard library types like `Vec<T>`
and `HashMap<K, V>`, as well as any structs or enums annotated with
`#[derive(Deserialize)]`.

Once we have `p` of type `Person`, our IDE and the Rust compiler can help us
use it correctly like they do for any other Rust code. The IDE can
autocomplete field names to prevent typos, which was impossible in the
`serde_json::Value` representation. And the Rust compiler can check that
when we write `p.phones[0]`, then `p.phones` is guaranteed to be a
`Vec<String>` so indexing into it makes sense and produces a `String`.

[§](https://docs.rs#constructing-json-values)Constructing JSON values

Serde JSON provides a [ json! macro](https://docs.rs/macro.json.html) to build

`serde_json::Value`
objects with very natural JSON syntax.```
use serde_json::json;
fn main() {
    // The type of `john` is `serde_json::Value`
    let john = json!({
        "name": "John Doe",
        "age": 43,
        "phones": [
            "+44 1234567",
            "+44 2345678"
        ]
    });
    println!("first phone number: {}", john["phones"][0]);
    // Convert to a string of JSON and print it out
    println!("{}", john.to_string());
}
```
The `Value::to_string()` function converts a `serde_json::Value` into a
`String` of JSON text.

One neat thing about the `json!` macro is that variables and expressions can
be interpolated directly into the JSON value as you are building it. Serde
will check at compile time that the value you are interpolating is able to
be represented as JSON.

```
let full_name = "John Doe";
let age_last_year = 42;
// The type of `john` is `serde_json::Value`
let john = json!({
    "name": full_name,
    "age": age_last_year + 1,
    "phones": [
        format!("+44 {}", random_phone())
    ]
});
```
This is amazingly convenient, but we have the problem we had before with
`Value`: the IDE and Rust compiler cannot help us if we get it wrong. Serde
JSON provides a better way of serializing strongly-typed data structures
into JSON text.

[§](https://docs.rs#creating-json-by-serializing-data-structures)Creating JSON by serializing data structures

A data structure can be converted to a JSON string by
[ serde_json::to_string](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string.html). There is also

[which serializes to a](https://docs.rs/fn.to_vec.html)

`serde_json::to_vec``Vec<u8>` and
[which serializes to any](https://docs.rs/fn.to_writer.html)

`serde_json::to_writer``io::Write`
such as a File or a TCP stream.```
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Result;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Address {
    street: String,
    city: String,
}
fn print_an_address() -> Result<()> {
    // Some data structure.
    let address = Address {
        street: "10 Downing Street".to_owned(),
        city: "London".to_owned(),
    };
    // Serialize it to a JSON string.
    let j = serde_json::to_string(&address)?;
    // Print, write to a file, or send to an HTTP server.
    println!("{}", j);
    Ok(())
}
```
Any type that implements Serde’s `Serialize` trait can be serialized this
way. This includes built-in Rust standard library types like `Vec<T>` and
`HashMap<K, V>`, as well as any structs or enums annotated with
`#[derive(Serialize)]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

As long as there is a memory allocator, it is possible to use serde_json without the rest of the Rust standard library. Disable the default “std” feature and enable the “alloc” feature:

```
[dependencies]
serde_json = { version = "1.0", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }
```
For JSON support in Serde without a memory allocator, please see the
[ serde-json-core](https://github.com/rust-embedded-community/serde-json-core) crate.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Deserialize JSON data to a Rust data structure.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- When serializing or deserializing JSON goes wrong.
- [map](https://docs.rs/map/index.html)
- A map of String to serde_json::Value.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)- `std`
- Serialize a Rust data structure into JSON data.
- [value](https://docs.rs/value/index.html)
- The Value enum, a loosely typed way of representing any valid JSON value.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- Construct a `serde_json::Value`from a JSON literal.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/struct.Deserializer.html)
- A structure that deserializes JSON into Rust values.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- This type represents all possible errors that can occur when serializing or deserializing JSON data.
- [Map](https://docs.rs/struct.Map.html)
- Represents a JSON key/value type.
- [Number](https://docs.rs/struct.Number.html)
- Represents a JSON number, whether integer or floating point.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/struct.Serializer.html)- `std`
- A structure for serializing Rust values into JSON.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamDeserializer.html)- Deserializer
- Iterator that deserializes a stream into multiple JSON values.

- Represents any valid JSON value.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string.html)- string - `std`
- Serialize the given data structure as a String of JSON.

- Serialize the given data structure as a pretty-printed String of JSON.

# xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-backend/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_backend/

## Expand description

Backend trait — code-lane emission abstraction.

Every target language in xpile (Rust, Ruchy, PTX, WGSL, SPIR-V, Lean)
provides one type implementing [ Backend](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html). The trait is intentionally
narrow: take meta-HIR and a config, return an

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Artifact.html)

`Artifact`Sibling of `xpile-frontend::Frontend`. Architectural invariants
codified in `contracts/xpile-backend-trait-v1.yaml`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Artifact](https://docs.rs/struct.Artifact.html)
- Emitted artifact — primary source/IR text plus sidecar files plus the structural citation chain to Layer-5 compile contracts.
- [Backend](https://docs.rs/struct.BackendConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration passed to `Backend::lower`
- [Emitted](https://docs.rs/struct.EmittedText.html)- Text
- Plain text emitted by a single `TargetEmitter``Artifact``QuorumStatus`(that’s chosen by the wrapper).
- [Multi](https://docs.rs/struct.MultiEmitterBackend.html)- Emitter - Backend
- Multi-emitter backend wrapper. Composes a general emitter
(mandatory) + an optional specialist under a `QuorumPolicy``Backend``TranspileSession`.
- [ViaEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.ViaEntry.html)
- A single emitter entry from `compile_targets.via`in the YAML schema. Mirrors the structured-record form spec’d in`sub/layer5-multi-emitter-quorum.md`§“Contract YAML schema extension”.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Backend](https://docs.rs/enum.BackendError.html)- Error
- [Diff](https://docs.rs/enum.DiffExecResult.html)- Exec - Result
- Result of a `DiffExec`quorum policy execution. Two PTX (or WGSL/ SPIR-V) programs were run on test inputs; the engine compared their numerical outputs.
- [Emitter](https://docs.rs/enum.EmitterRole.html)- Role
- Role of a backend emitter within a multi-emitter quorum.
- [HwProfile](https://docs.rs/enum.HwProfile.html)
- Hardware profile for targets whose emission depends on hardware
capabilities (PTX `compute_capability`, WGSL feature set, SPIR-V version).
- [Profile](https://docs.rs/enum.Profile.html)
- Lowering profile — the two-mHIR asymmetric decision for Rust↔Ruchy.
- [Quorum](https://docs.rs/enum.QuorumPolicy.html)- Policy
- Policy for combining outputs when both General and Specialist
emitters fire on the same input. Configured per Layer-5 contract
via `compile_targets.quorum_policy`in the YAML.
- [Quorum](https://docs.rs/enum.QuorumStatus.html)- Status
- Status of a multi-emitter quorum vote, attached to an `Artifact`
- [Target](https://docs.rs/enum.Target.html)
- Target language a backend can emit.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Backend](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html)
- Code-lane emission trait. See `docs/specifications/sub/backend-trait.md`.
- [Diff](https://docs.rs/trait.DiffExecEngine.html)- Exec - Engine
- PMAT-486 (§30 Track 4): engine that executes two emitted programs on contract-fixture inputs and numerically compares the outputs within a tolerance — the Runtime-stratum half of the §29 quorum. The trait + hook land here (free CI); the real CUDA / Vulkan implementations (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) run out-of-band on self-hosted GPU runners.
- [Target](https://docs.rs/trait.TargetEmitter.html)- Emitter
- Single-emitter trait — sub-trait of a multi-emitter backend.
One `TargetEmitter``MultiEmitterBackend`

[16](https://docs.rs#16)pub enum Target {
[17](https://docs.rs#17)    /// Idiomatic Rust source. Implemented by `xpile-rust-codegen`.
[18](https://docs.rs#18)    Rust,
[19](https://docs.rs#19)    /// Ruchy source. Implemented by `xpile-ruchy-codegen`.
[20](https://docs.rs#20)    Ruchy,
[21](https://docs.rs#21)    /// NVIDIA PTX text. Implemented by `xpile-ptx-codegen`.
[22](https://docs.rs#22)    Ptx,
[23](https://docs.rs#23)    /// WebGPU Shading Language. Implemented by `xpile-wgsl-codegen`.
[24](https://docs.rs#24)    Wgsl,
[25](https://docs.rs#25)    /// SPIR-V — the native Vulkan IR. Implemented by `xpile-spirv-codegen`
[26](https://docs.rs#26)    /// (PMAT-960). REUSES the WGSL emission and compiles it WGSL→naga→spv
[27](https://docs.rs#27)    /// (NOT a hand-written SPIR-V assembler); the §29 cross-emitter witness
[28](https://docs.rs#28)    /// RUNS the emitted SPIR-V on a real wgpu Vulkan adapter. The native-IR
[29](https://docs.rs#29)    /// sibling of `Target::Wgsl`.
[30](https://docs.rs#30)    Spirv,
[31](https://docs.rs#31)    /// WebAssembly Text format (WAT). Implemented by `xpile-wasm-codegen`.
[32](https://docs.rs#32)    /// The EMIT half of first-class bidirectional native WASM (PMAT-951) —
[33](https://docs.rs#33)    /// lowers the meta-HIR scalar/control subset directly to WAT text, NOT
[34](https://docs.rs#34)    /// via the Ruchy `WasmEmitter` hop. See `project-bidirectional-wasm`.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)    Wasm,
[36](https://docs.rs#36)    /// Lean 4 executable code (def, partial def, inductive, ...).
[37](https://docs.rs#37)    /// Implemented by `xpile-lean-codegen`. The proof-lane Lean (theorems)
[38](https://docs.rs#38)    /// goes through `xpile-lean-contract-backend` instead.
[39](https://docs.rs#39)    Lean,
[40](https://docs.rs#40)    /// POSIX shell (sh / bash / zsh) — the bashrs merger domain.
[41](https://docs.rs#41)    /// Implemented by `bashrs-backend` (scaffold at v0.1.0; full emit
[42](https://docs.rs#42)    /// at v0.2.0 once the bashrs source folding lands). PMAT-037 /
[43](https://docs.rs#43)    /// XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001. See `sub/bashrs-merger.md` Layer A.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)    Shell,
[45](https://docs.rs#45)    /// forjar.yaml IaC manifest text. Implemented by
[46](https://docs.rs#46)    /// `xpile-forjar-codegen` (PMAT-953). The BACKEND-ONLY forjar
[47](https://docs.rs#47)    /// integration (NOT merge/federate) — a declarative ops/deployment
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    /// output lane, peer to bashrs-backend's shell lane. Lowers a
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    /// SHELL-origin meta-HIR `Module` (the `Stmt::Cmd` / `Stmt::Pipeline`
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    /// command sequence) to forjar `type: file` / `type: task` resources.
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    /// REFUSES non-shell modules and any shell idempotence guard /
[52](https://docs.rs#52)    /// conditional (the meta-HIR shell lane has no `Stmt::ShellIf`), so
[53](https://docs.rs#53)    /// only unconditional resources emit — forjar re-adds convergence at
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    /// apply time. See `project-forjar-output-backend`.
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    ForjarYaml,
[56](https://docs.rs#56)}
[57](https://docs.rs#57)
[58](https://docs.rs#58)/// Lowering profile — the two-mHIR asymmetric decision for Rust↔Ruchy.

[60](https://docs.rs#60)/// See `docs/specifications/sub/bidirectional-ruchy.md` (planned).
[61](https://docs.rs#61)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

[63](https://docs.rs#63)    /// meta-HIR normalized for Rust emission (default for most targets).
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    RustOut,

[66](https://docs.rs#66)    /// reconstructed at emission time).
[67](https://docs.rs#67)    RuchyOut,
[68](https://docs.rs#68)}

[112](https://docs.rs#112)    pub citations: Vec<ContractId>,
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    /// Multi-emitter quorum status (PMAT-262 / Section 29). At v0.1.0

[115](https://docs.rs#115)    /// `QuorumStatus::Single { emitter: <backend_name> }`. Multi-emitter
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// backends (future rustc_codegen_nvvm + aprender-gpu quorum on PTX)
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    /// populate `QuorumStatus::Multi { ... }` with the diff_exec result.
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    ///
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    /// Defaults via serde to `Single { emitter: "unknown" }` for
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    /// backward-compatible deserialization of older JSON payloads.

[145](https://docs.rs#145)    /// Human-readable backend name, e.g. "rust", "ptx", "wgsl".
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
[147](https://docs.rs#147)

[149](https://docs.rs#149)    /// owned by exactly one Backend impl (`target_ownership` invariant).
[150](https://docs.rs#150)    fn targets(&self) -> &[Target];
[151](https://docs.rs#151)
[152](https://docs.rs#152)    /// Lower a meta-HIR module under the given config to an [`Artifact`].
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    ///
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    /// Invariants: deterministic per `(module, config)`; frame-pure
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    /// (no mutation of inputs); every target-specific IR construct
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    /// in `Artifact.primary` cited via `Artifact.citations`.
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    fn lower(&self, module: &Module, config: &BackendConfig) -> Result<Artifact, BackendError>;

[163](https://docs.rs#163)// `docs/specifications/sub/layer5-multi-emitter-quorum.md`. Pure
[164](https://docs.rs#164)// scaffolding at PMAT-261 — no Backend impl yet uses these. Future PRs
[165](https://docs.rs#165)// (rustc_codegen_nvvm wiring, aprender-gpu bridge, DiffExec engine)
[166](https://docs.rs#166)// build against this stable API surface.
[167](https://docs.rs#167)
[168](https://docs.rs#168)/// Role of a backend emitter within a multi-emitter quorum.
[169](https://docs.rs#169)///
[170](https://docs.rs#170)/// `compile_targets.via.role` in the YAML schema corresponds to this
[171](https://docs.rs#171)/// enum. At most one `General` per quorum (the mandatory fallback);
[172](https://docs.rs#172)/// any number of `Specialist` (each with its own `shape_filter`).
[173](https://docs.rs#173)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[174](https://docs.rs#174)#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
[175](https://docs.rs#175)pub enum EmitterRole {
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// Handles any contract-conforming input. Mandatory fallback —
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    /// `pv lint` (post-PMAT-262) will require at least one `General`
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    /// emitter per Layer-5 contract's `compile_targets.via`.
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    /// Examples: `rustc_codegen_nvvm` (PTX), `naga` (WGSL),
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    /// `rspirv` (SPIR-V).
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    General,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    /// Handles a domain-specific subset via hand-tuned templates.
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    /// Optional — degrades gracefully to single-emitter when missing.
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    /// Examples: `aprender-gpu` (GEMM/MMA PTX kernels),
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    /// `bashrs-realistic` (corpus-tuned POSIX patterns).
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    Specialist,
[187](https://docs.rs#187)}
[188](https://docs.rs#188)
[189](https://docs.rs#189)/// Policy for combining outputs when both General and Specialist
[190](https://docs.rs#190)/// emitters fire on the same input. Configured per Layer-5 contract
[191](https://docs.rs#191)/// via `compile_targets.quorum_policy` in the YAML.
[192](https://docs.rs#192)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[193](https://docs.rs#193)#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "kind")]
[194](https://docs.rs#194)pub enum QuorumPolicy {
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// If the specialist handles the kernel, use its output. Falls
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    /// back to general otherwise. Single-vote Runtime stratum.
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    PreferSpecialist,
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    /// Emit via BOTH, run BOTH on test inputs, compare numerical
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// outputs within tolerance. Multi-vote Runtime stratum.
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// **Falsifies the contract on divergence** — this is the
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// stratum-upgrading policy that closes the §4 "Run=1 demo
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// fixture" caveat from audit-design.md.
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    DiffExec {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)        /// Maximum allowed absolute difference between corresponding
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        /// numerical outputs of the two emitters.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)        tolerance: f64,
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    },
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    /// Strict text-equality between PTX outputs. Useful for
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// regression-locking, NOT for falsification — different valid
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// PTX programs commonly produce identical execution results via
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// different instruction sequences.
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    Strict,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)}
[214](https://docs.rs#214)
[215](https://docs.rs#215)/// Status of a multi-emitter quorum vote, attached to an [`Artifact`]
[216](https://docs.rs#216)/// produced by a multi-emitter backend.
[217](https://docs.rs#217)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[218](https://docs.rs#218)#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
[219](https://docs.rs#219)pub enum QuorumStatus {
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// Only one emitter fired (specialist missing for this shape, or
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    /// quorum policy is `PreferSpecialist` and specialist matched).
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// Runtime stratum vote count: 1.
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    Single { emitter: String },
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// Both emitters fired; outputs were combined under the policy.
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// Runtime stratum vote count: 2.
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    Multi {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)        emitters: Vec<String>,
[228](https://docs.rs#228)        diff_exec: Option<DiffExecResult>,
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    },
[230](https://docs.rs#230)}
[231](https://docs.rs#231)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)/// Result of a `DiffExec` quorum policy execution. Two PTX (or WGSL/
[233](https://docs.rs#233)/// SPIR-V) programs were run on test inputs; the engine compared
[234](https://docs.rs#234)/// their numerical outputs.
[235](https://docs.rs#235)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[236](https://docs.rs#236)#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
[237](https://docs.rs#237)pub enum DiffExecResult {
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    /// Outputs matched within tolerance. Records the max absolute
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// difference observed for audit trail.
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    Match { max_abs_diff: f64 },
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    /// Outputs diverged beyond tolerance. **Contract violation** —
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    /// CI fails. Records the divergence for diagnosis.
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    Divergent { max_abs_diff: f64, tolerance: f64 },
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    /// Engine did not run (e.g., test hardware unavailable). Vote
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    /// downgrades from Runtime to a placeholder. The substrate
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    /// records this rather than silently dropping it.
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    NotRun { reason: String },
[248](https://docs.rs#248)}
[249](https://docs.rs#249)
[250](https://docs.rs#250)/// A single emitter entry from `compile_targets.via` in the YAML

[253](https://docs.rs#253)///
[254](https://docs.rs#254)/// At v0.1.0 the YAML schema is still a flat `[String]`; this struct

[256](https://docs.rs#256)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[257](https://docs.rs#257)pub struct ViaEntry {

[259](https://docs.rs#259)    pub emitter: String,
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    /// Role within the quorum.
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    pub role: EmitterRole,
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    /// Local crate that registers this emitter (for `role: general`).
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    pub crate_name: Option<String>,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    /// Cross-repo binding target (for `role: specialist` cases where

[267](https://docs.rs#267)    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    pub cross_repo: Option<String>,
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// Optional shape filter — for specialists, identifies which
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// input shapes this emitter handles. Tied to a sub-contract
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    /// (e.g., `gemm_fp16_mma_64x128` matches aprender's
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// `C-COMPUTE-GEMM-FP16-MMA` contract).
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    pub shape_filter: Option<String>,
[275](https://docs.rs#275)}

[277](https://docs.rs#277)// ─── PMAT-263 / Section 29: TargetEmitter trait + MultiEmitterBackend ────
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//
[279](https://docs.rs#279)// Routing layer for multi-emitter backends. A [`MultiEmitterBackend`]
[280](https://docs.rs#280)// composes a general emitter (mandatory fallback) + an optional
[281](https://docs.rs#281)// specialist emitter under a [`QuorumPolicy`]. Single-emitter and
[282](https://docs.rs#282)// multi-emitter cases produce explicit `QuorumStatus` on the emitted
[283](https://docs.rs#283)// [`Artifact`].
[284](https://docs.rs#284)
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// Plain text emitted by a single [`TargetEmitter`] before the
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// multi-emitter routing decides what to put in the final [`Artifact`].
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// Doesn't carry `QuorumStatus` (that's chosen by the wrapper).
[288](https://docs.rs#288)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[289](https://docs.rs#289)pub struct EmittedText {
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    pub primary: String,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    pub citations: Vec<ContractId>,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)}
[294](https://docs.rs#294)
[295](https://docs.rs#295)/// Single-emitter trait — sub-trait of a multi-emitter backend.
[296](https://docs.rs#296)/// One [`TargetEmitter`] handles emission for one logical path
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// (general vs specialist). Each [`MultiEmitterBackend`] wraps
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// one mandatory general emitter and optionally one specialist.
[299](https://docs.rs#299)pub trait TargetEmitter: Send + Sync {
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    /// Human-readable emitter name (used in [`QuorumStatus`]).
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    fn name(&self) -> &str;
[302](https://docs.rs#302)
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    /// Attempt to emit for this input. Specialists return `None`
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    /// when their shape filter doesn't match — the wrapper then
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    /// uses only the general emitter. General emitters should
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// always return `Some(...)` for any contract-conforming input.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    fn try_emit(
[308](https://docs.rs#308)        &self,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)        module: &Module,
[310](https://docs.rs#310)        config: &BackendConfig,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>>;
[312](https://docs.rs#312)}
[313](https://docs.rs#313)
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// PMAT-486 (§30 Track 4): engine that executes two emitted programs on
[315](https://docs.rs#315)/// contract-fixture inputs and numerically compares the outputs within a
[316](https://docs.rs#316)/// tolerance — the Runtime-stratum half of the §29 quorum. The trait +
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// hook land here (free CI); the real CUDA / Vulkan implementations
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) run out-of-band on self-hosted GPU runners.
[319](https://docs.rs#319)///
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// Error posture (per the §30 Track-4 review): with **no engine
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// installed** the `DiffExec` policy records `NotRun { reason: no-engine }`
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// (benign — free CI stays green). An **installed** engine that returns
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// `Err` propagates a hard [`BackendError`] that fails the job — a broken
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// GPU run must NOT masquerade as "not run".
[325](https://docs.rs#325)pub trait DiffExecEngine: Send + Sync {
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// Execute `general_text` and `specialist_text` on the contract's
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// fixture inputs and compare. `Ok(Match|Divergent)` records the
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    /// vote; `Err(msg)` is a hard failure (e.g. driver fault / launch
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    /// error) the caller turns into a `BackendError`.
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    fn execute_and_compare(
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        &self,
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        general_text: &str,
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        specialist_text: &str,
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        module: &Module,
[335](https://docs.rs#335)        config: &BackendConfig,
[336](https://docs.rs#336)        tolerance: f64,
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    ) -> Result<DiffExecResult, String>;
[338](https://docs.rs#338)}
[339](https://docs.rs#339)
[340](https://docs.rs#340)/// Multi-emitter backend wrapper. Composes a general emitter
[341](https://docs.rs#341)/// (mandatory) + an optional specialist under a [`QuorumPolicy`].
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// Implements [`Backend`] so it slots into the existing dispatch
[343](https://docs.rs#343)/// without touching `TranspileSession`.
[344](https://docs.rs#344)pub struct MultiEmitterBackend {
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    /// Single target this multi-emitter backend serves
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    /// (e.g., [`Target::Ptx`]).
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    pub target: Target,
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    /// Mandatory general emitter. Must handle any
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    /// contract-conforming input as a fallback.
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    pub general: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>,
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    /// Optional specialist emitter. Returns `None` from `try_emit`
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// when its shape filter doesn't match the input.
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    pub specialist: Option<Box<dyn TargetEmitter>>,
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    /// How to combine outputs when both emitters fire.
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    pub quorum_policy: QuorumPolicy,
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    /// PMAT-486: optional `DiffExec` execution engine. `None` (the
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    /// default) records `NotRun { no-engine }` under `QuorumPolicy::
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    /// DiffExec`; `Some(engine)` runs the Runtime-stratum comparison.
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    pub diff_exec_engine: Option<std::sync::Arc<dyn DiffExecEngine>>,
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    /// PMAT-1006: names of ADDITIONAL categorically-independent emitters the
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    /// installed `DiffExec` engine runs INTERNALLY beyond `general`+`specialist`
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    /// (e.g. the PTX §29 3-way quorum's `rustc-nvptx` arm, self-generated inside
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    /// the engine). When the engine reports a `Match`/`Divergent` (i.e. it
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    /// actually executed), these are appended to the reported `emitters` list so
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    /// `QuorumStatus::Multi` HONESTLY names every toolchain that voted. Empty for
[366](https://docs.rs#366)    /// every other backend (no behaviour change).
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    pub diff_exec_extra_emitters: Vec<String>,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)}
[369](https://docs.rs#369)
[370](https://docs.rs#370)impl MultiEmitterBackend {
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    pub fn new_single(target: Target, general: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>) -> Self {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)        Self {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            target,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            general,
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            specialist: None,
[376](https://docs.rs#376)            quorum_policy: QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist,
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            diff_exec_engine: None,
[378](https://docs.rs#378)            diff_exec_extra_emitters: Vec::new(),
[379](https://docs.rs#379)        }
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    }
[381](https://docs.rs#381)
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    pub fn new_with_specialist(
[383](https://docs.rs#383)        target: Target,
[384](https://docs.rs#384)        general: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>,
[385](https://docs.rs#385)        specialist: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>,
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        quorum_policy: QuorumPolicy,
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    ) -> Self {
[388](https://docs.rs#388)        Self {
[389](https://docs.rs#389)            target,
[390](https://docs.rs#390)            general,
[391](https://docs.rs#391)            specialist: Some(specialist),
[392](https://docs.rs#392)            quorum_policy,
[393](https://docs.rs#393)            diff_exec_engine: None,
[394](https://docs.rs#394)            diff_exec_extra_emitters: Vec::new(),
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    }
[397](https://docs.rs#397)
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// PMAT-486: install a `DiffExec` engine (builder style). The real
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// CUDA / Vulkan engines (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) plug in here on the
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// self-hosted GPU runners; on free CI the engine stays `None`.
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    pub fn with_diff_exec_engine(mut self, engine: std::sync::Arc<dyn DiffExecEngine>) -> Self {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)        self.diff_exec_engine = Some(engine);
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        self
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// PMAT-1006: declare additional emitters the installed `DiffExec` engine
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    /// runs internally (beyond general+specialist), so an EXECUTED `Multi`
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    /// result names every toolchain that voted (the PTX 3-way §29 quorum).
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    pub fn with_diff_exec_extra_emitters(mut self, names: Vec<String>) -> Self {
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        self.diff_exec_extra_emitters = names;
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        self
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    }
[413](https://docs.rs#413)}
[414](https://docs.rs#414)
[415](https://docs.rs#415)impl Backend for MultiEmitterBackend {
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        // The wrapper name is generic; per-emitter names live in
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        // QuorumStatus on each emitted Artifact for audit recovery.
[419](https://docs.rs#419)        "multi-emitter"
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    }
[421](https://docs.rs#421)
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    fn targets(&self) -> &[Target] {
[423](https://docs.rs#423)        std::slice::from_ref(&self.target)
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    }
[425](https://docs.rs#425)
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    fn lower(&self, module: &Module, config: &BackendConfig) -> Result<Artifact, BackendError> {
[427](https://docs.rs#427)        let general_result = self.general.try_emit(module, config).ok_or_else(|| {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)            BackendError::Lower(format!(
[429](https://docs.rs#429)                "general emitter {} must always match contract-conforming input",
[430](https://docs.rs#430)                self.general.name()
[431](https://docs.rs#431)            ))
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        })??;
[433](https://docs.rs#433)
[434](https://docs.rs#434)        let specialist_result = self.specialist.as_ref().and_then(|s| {
[435](https://docs.rs#435)            s.try_emit(module, config)
[436](https://docs.rs#436)                .map(|r| (s.name().to_string(), r))
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        });
[438](https://docs.rs#438)
[439](https://docs.rs#439)        match specialist_result {
[440](https://docs.rs#440)            None => {
[441](https://docs.rs#441)                // Only general fired — Single-vote Runtime stratum.
[442](https://docs.rs#442)                Ok(Artifact {
[443](https://docs.rs#443)                    primary: general_result.primary,
[444](https://docs.rs#444)                    sidecars: Vec::new(),
[445](https://docs.rs#445)                    citations: general_result.citations,
[446](https://docs.rs#446)                    quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Single {
[447](https://docs.rs#447)                        emitter: self.general.name().to_string(),
[448](https://docs.rs#448)                    },
[449](https://docs.rs#449)                })
[450](https://docs.rs#450)            }
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            Some((specialist_name, specialist_emit)) => {
[452](https://docs.rs#452)                let specialist_text = specialist_emit?;
[453](https://docs.rs#453)                match &self.quorum_policy {
[454](https://docs.rs#454)                    QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist => {
[455](https://docs.rs#455)                        // Use specialist's output; general was emitted for
[456](https://docs.rs#456)                        // sanity but isn't reported as a vote.
[457](https://docs.rs#457)                        Ok(Artifact {
[458](https://docs.rs#458)                            primary: specialist_text.primary,
[459](https://docs.rs#459)                            sidecars: Vec::new(),
[460](https://docs.rs#460)                            citations: specialist_text.citations,
[461](https://docs.rs#461)                            quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Single {
[462](https://docs.rs#462)                                emitter: specialist_name,
[463](https://docs.rs#463)                            },
[464](https://docs.rs#464)                        })
[465](https://docs.rs#465)                    }
[466](https://docs.rs#466)                    QuorumPolicy::Strict => {
[467](https://docs.rs#467)                        // Text-equality check.
[468](https://docs.rs#468)                        let diff_exec = if general_result.primary == specialist_text.primary {
[469](https://docs.rs#469)                            Some(DiffExecResult::Match { max_abs_diff: 0.0 })
[470](https://docs.rs#470)                        } else {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)                            Some(DiffExecResult::Divergent {
[472](https://docs.rs#472)                                max_abs_diff: f64::INFINITY,
[473](https://docs.rs#473)                                tolerance: 0.0,
[474](https://docs.rs#474)                            })
[475](https://docs.rs#475)                        };
[476](https://docs.rs#476)                        Ok(Artifact {
[477](https://docs.rs#477)                            primary: general_result.primary.clone(),
[478](https://docs.rs#478)                            sidecars: vec![(
[479](https://docs.rs#479)                                "specialist_emission".to_string(),
[480](https://docs.rs#480)                                specialist_text.primary.into_bytes(),
[481](https://docs.rs#481)                            )],
[482](https://docs.rs#482)                            citations: general_result.citations,
[483](https://docs.rs#483)                            quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Multi {
[484](https://docs.rs#484)                                emitters: vec![self.general.name().to_string(), specialist_name],
[485](https://docs.rs#485)                                diff_exec,
[486](https://docs.rs#486)                            },
[487](https://docs.rs#487)                        })
[488](https://docs.rs#488)                    }
[489](https://docs.rs#489)                    QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance } => {
[490](https://docs.rs#490)                        // PMAT-486: run the installed engine, or record
[491](https://docs.rs#491)                        // NotRun{no-engine} when none is installed (free
[492](https://docs.rs#492)                        // CI). An installed engine that errors propagates
[493](https://docs.rs#493)                        // a hard BackendError — a broken GPU run must NOT
[494](https://docs.rs#494)                        // masquerade as "not run".
[495](https://docs.rs#495)                        let diff_exec = match &self.diff_exec_engine {
[496](https://docs.rs#496)                            Some(engine) => engine
[497](https://docs.rs#497)                                .execute_and_compare(
[498](https://docs.rs#498)                                    &general_result.primary,
[499](https://docs.rs#499)                                    &specialist_text.primary,
[500](https://docs.rs#500)                                    module,
[501](https://docs.rs#501)                                    config,
[502](https://docs.rs#502)                                    *tolerance,
[503](https://docs.rs#503)                                )
[504](https://docs.rs#504)                                .map_err(|e| {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)                                    BackendError::Lower(format!(
[506](https://docs.rs#506)                                        "DiffExec engine for {:?} failed: {e}",
[507](https://docs.rs#507)                                        self.target
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                                    ))
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                                })?,
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                            None => DiffExecResult::NotRun {
[511](https://docs.rs#511)                                reason: format!(
[512](https://docs.rs#512)                                    "no DiffExec engine installed (tolerance was {tolerance})"
[513](https://docs.rs#513)                                ),
[514](https://docs.rs#514)                            },
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                        };
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                        // PMAT-1006: the base voters are general + specialist.
[517](https://docs.rs#517)                        // When the engine actually EXECUTED (Match/Divergent, not
[518](https://docs.rs#518)                        // NotRun), append the extra toolchains it ran internally
[519](https://docs.rs#519)                        // (e.g. the PTX 3-way `rustc-nvptx` arm) so the reported
[520](https://docs.rs#520)                        // quorum HONESTLY names every voter. A non-executed run
[521](https://docs.rs#521)                        // (NotRun, no GPU) reports only the emitters that fired.
[522](https://docs.rs#522)                        let mut emitters = vec![self.general.name().to_string(), specialist_name];
[523](https://docs.rs#523)                        if matches!(
[524](https://docs.rs#524)                            diff_exec,
[525](https://docs.rs#525)                            DiffExecResult::Match { .. } | DiffExecResult::Divergent { .. }
[526](https://docs.rs#526)                        ) {
[527](https://docs.rs#527)                            emitters.extend(self.diff_exec_extra_emitters.iter().cloned());
[528](https://docs.rs#528)                        }
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                        Ok(Artifact {
[530](https://docs.rs#530)                            primary: general_result.primary.clone(),
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                            sidecars: vec![(
[532](https://docs.rs#532)                                "specialist_emission".to_string(),
[533](https://docs.rs#533)                                specialist_text.primary.into_bytes(),
[534](https://docs.rs#534)                            )],
[535](https://docs.rs#535)                            citations: general_result.citations,
[536](https://docs.rs#536)                            quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Multi {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)                                emitters,
[538](https://docs.rs#538)                                diff_exec: Some(diff_exec),
[539](https://docs.rs#539)                            },
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                        })
[541](https://docs.rs#541)                    }
[542](https://docs.rs#542)                }
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            }
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        }

[886](https://docs.rs#886)    // ─── PMAT-266: Adversarial invariants for MultiEmitterBackend ───
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    //
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    // These tests pin down security-relevant contract behavior that the
[889](https://docs.rs#889)    // PMAT-263 happy-path tests don't cover: citation provenance, error
[890](https://docs.rs#890)    // propagation, hidden-divergence documentation, and observability of
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    // the `NotRun` reason. They guard against silent regressions in the
[892](https://docs.rs#892)    // routing layer that would weaken the Section 29 oracle.
[893](https://docs.rs#893)
[894](https://docs.rs#894)    /// Mock emitter with configurable citations — used to verify which
[895](https://docs.rs#895)    /// emitter's citations end up in the final Artifact.
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    struct MockGeneralWithCitations {
[897](https://docs.rs#897)        body: String,
[898](https://docs.rs#898)        citations: Vec<ContractId>,
[899](https://docs.rs#899)    }
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    impl TargetEmitter for MockGeneralWithCitations {
[901](https://docs.rs#901)        fn name(&self) -> &str {
[902](https://docs.rs#902)            "general-with-cites"
[903](https://docs.rs#903)        }
[904](https://docs.rs#904)        fn try_emit(
[905](https://docs.rs#905)            &self,
[906](https://docs.rs#906)            _module: &Module,
[907](https://docs.rs#907)            _config: &BackendConfig,
[908](https://docs.rs#908)        ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>> {
[909](https://docs.rs#909)            Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[910](https://docs.rs#910)                primary: self.body.clone(),
[911](https://docs.rs#911)                citations: self.citations.clone(),
[912](https://docs.rs#912)            }))
[913](https://docs.rs#913)        }
[914](https://docs.rs#914)    }
[915](https://docs.rs#915)

[974](https://docs.rs#974)    #[test]
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    fn strict_divergence_preserves_general_citations_not_specialist() {
[976](https://docs.rs#976)        // Security invariant: under `Strict`, citations come from
[977](https://docs.rs#977)        // `general`. The proof lane relies on this — citations identify
[978](https://docs.rs#978)        // which contracts the artifact was authored against. A
[979](https://docs.rs#979)        // specialist that disagrees with general must not be able to
[980](https://docs.rs#980)        // silently swap its own citations into the audit trail.
[981](https://docs.rs#981)        let backend = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[982](https://docs.rs#982)            Target::Ptx,
[983](https://docs.rs#983)            Box::new(MockGeneralWithCitations {
[984](https://docs.rs#984)                body: "general output".into(),
[985](https://docs.rs#985)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-GENERAL-CITED")],
[986](https://docs.rs#986)            }),
[987](https://docs.rs#987)            Box::new(MockSpecialistWithCitations {
[988](https://docs.rs#988)                body: "different output".into(),
[989](https://docs.rs#989)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-SPECIALIST-CITED")],
[990](https://docs.rs#990)            }),
[991](https://docs.rs#991)            QuorumPolicy::Strict,
[992](https://docs.rs#992)        );
[993](https://docs.rs#993)        let artifact = backend.lower(&dummy_module(), &dummy_config()).unwrap();
[994](https://docs.rs#994)        assert_eq!(artifact.citations.len(), 1);
[995](https://docs.rs#995)        assert_eq!(artifact.citations[0].as_str(), "C-GENERAL-CITED");
[996](https://docs.rs#996)        // Specialist's body is still recoverable from the sidecar even
[997](https://docs.rs#997)        // though its citations are dropped.
[998](https://docs.rs#998)        assert_eq!(artifact.sidecars.len(), 1);
[999](https://docs.rs#999)        assert_eq!(
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)            artifact.sidecars[0].1,
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)            b"different output".to_vec(),
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)            "specialist body should be preserved in sidecar"
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)        );
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)    }

[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)    #[test]
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)    fn prefer_specialist_hides_divergence_by_design() {
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)        // Documented trade-off: `PreferSpecialist` is the
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)        // single-vote-runtime stratum — it intentionally does NOT
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)        // compare general vs specialist. Use `Strict` or `DiffExec`
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)        // when divergence detection matters. This test pins down the
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)        // behavior so a future "helpful" refactor can't accidentally
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)        // turn this into a quiet divergence detector.
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)        let backend = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)            Target::Ptx,
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)            Box::new(MockGeneralWithCitations {
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)                body: "general thinks the answer is 42".into(),
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-GENERAL")],
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)            }),
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)            Box::new(MockSpecialistWithCitations {
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)                body: "specialist thinks the answer is 99".into(),
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-SPECIALIST")],
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)            }),
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)            QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist,
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)        );
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)        let artifact = backend.lower(&dummy_module(), &dummy_config()).unwrap();
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)        // Specialist's body wins; specialist's citations win;
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)        // QuorumStatus reports Single (no divergence captured).
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)        assert!(artifact.primary.contains("99"));
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        assert_eq!(artifact.citations[0].as_str(), "C-SPECIALIST");
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)        match artifact.quorum_status {
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)            QuorumStatus::Single { emitter } => {
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)                assert_eq!(emitter, "specialist-with-cites");
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)            }
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)            other => panic!("expected Single quorum status, got {other:?}"),
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)        }
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)        // No sidecar — general's emission isn't even captured.
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)        assert!(artifact.sidecars.is_empty());
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)    }

[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)    #[test]
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)    fn diff_exec_does_not_short_circuit_on_text_equality() {
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)        // Architectural invariant: even when general and specialist
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        // emit byte-identical text, `DiffExec` policy must still
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)        // record `NotRun` (because the real engine compares numerical
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)        // outputs after execution, not source text). A future
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)        // optimization that says "skip diff if text matches" would
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)        // break this invariant — the engine's job is to check the
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)        // RUNTIME behavior, and identical source could still produce
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)        // divergent runtime values on different hardware.
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)        let backend = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)            Target::Ptx,
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)            Box::new(MockGeneral {
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)                name: "general",
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)                body: "byte identical".into(),
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)            }),
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)            Box::new(MockSpecialist {
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)                name: "specialist",
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)                matches: true,
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)                body: "byte identical".into(),
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)            }),
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)            QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance: 1e-6 },
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)        );
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)        let artifact = backend.lower(&dummy_module(), &dummy_config()).unwrap();
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)        match artifact.quorum_status {
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)            QuorumStatus::Multi { diff_exec, .. } => {
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)                assert!(
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)                    matches!(diff_exec, Some(DiffExecResult::NotRun { .. })),
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)                    "DiffExec policy must NOT short-circuit on text equality \
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)                     — engine compares runtime values, not source text"
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)                );
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)            }
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)            other => panic!("expected Multi quorum status, got {other:?}"),
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)        }
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)    }

[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)                ..
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)            } => assert!(reason.contains("no DiffExec engine"), "got: {reason}"),
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)            other => panic!("expected Multi NotRun, got {other:?}"),
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)        }
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)    }

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.diff_exec_extra_emitters)

installed `DiffExec` engine runs INTERNALLY beyond `general`+`specialist`
(e.g. the PTX §29 3-way quorum’s `rustc-nvptx` arm, self-generated inside
the engine). When the engine reports a `Match`/`Divergent` (i.e. it
actually executed), these are appended to the reported `emitters` list so
`QuorumStatus::Multi` HONESTLY names every toolchain that voted. Empty for
every other backend (no behaviour change).

# DiffExecResult in xpile_backend - Rust

```
pub enum DiffExecResult {
    Match {
        max_abs_diff:
```
[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    },
    Divergent {
        max_abs_diff: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
        tolerance: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    },
    NotRun {
        reason: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    },
}## Expand description

Result of a `DiffExec` quorum policy execution. Two PTX (or WGSL/
SPIR-V) programs were run on test inputs; the engine compared
their numerical outputs.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Match)

### Match

Outputs matched within tolerance. Records the max absolute difference observed for audit trail.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Divergent)

### Divergent

Outputs diverged beyond tolerance. **Contract violation** —
CI fails. Records the divergence for diagnosis.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NotRun)

### NotRun

Engine did not run (e.g., test hardware unavailable). Vote downgrades from Runtime to a placeholder. The substrate records this rather than silently dropping it.

# EmitterRole in xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/xpile_backend/enum.EmitterRole.html

```
pub enum EmitterRole {
    General,
    Specialist,
}
```
## Expand description

Role of a backend emitter within a multi-emitter quorum.

`compile_targets.via.role` in the YAML schema corresponds to this
enum. At most one `General` per quorum (the mandatory fallback);
any number of `Specialist` (each with its own `shape_filter`).

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.General)

### General

Handles any contract-conforming input. Mandatory fallback —
`pv lint` (post-PMAT-262) will require at least one `General`
emitter per Layer-5 contract’s `compile_targets.via`.
Examples: `rustc_codegen_nvvm` (PTX), `naga` (WGSL),
`rspirv` (SPIR-V).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Specialist)

### Specialist

Handles a domain-specific subset via hand-tuned templates.
Optional — degrades gracefully to single-emitter when missing.
Examples: `aprender-gpu` (GEMM/MMA PTX kernels),
`bashrs-realistic` (corpus-tuned POSIX patterns).

# DiffExecEngine in xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/xpile_backend/trait.DiffExecEngine.html

`pub trait DiffExecEngine: `[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [execute_and_compare](https://docs.rs#tymethod.execute_and_compare)(
        &self,
        general_text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
        specialist_text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
        module: &[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html),
        config: &[BackendConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.BackendConfig.html),
        tolerance: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[DiffExecResult](https://docs.rs/enum.DiffExecResult.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>;
}## Expand description

PMAT-486 (§30 Track 4): engine that executes two emitted programs on contract-fixture inputs and numerically compares the outputs within a tolerance — the Runtime-stratum half of the §29 quorum. The trait + hook land here (free CI); the real CUDA / Vulkan implementations (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) run out-of-band on self-hosted GPU runners.

Error posture (per the §30 Track-4 review): with **no engine
installed** the `DiffExec` policy records `NotRun { reason: no-engine }`
(benign — free CI stays green). An **installed** engine that returns
`Err` propagates a hard [ BackendError](https://docs.rs/enum.BackendError.html) that fails the job — a broken
GPU run must NOT masquerade as “not run”.
